Good game overall.
Can be a little unforgiving at times -keep tabs on that food supply! The mods certainly give the game a new lease of life but it can become quite samey after a while. Once you master the art of keeping a good balance of produce, food being the only critical one, theres not a lot to it. There are no objectives. Nothing is 'locked'. There are no enemies as such (natural disasters the exception) There are no real boundaries. If you build the most succsessful town in history with 1000+ inhabitants totally self sufficient - nobody will care. There is no end, it just goes on until you are too bored to continue.
A decent choice of building options and loads of different produce routes to explore. A fair amount of choice for starting options and climate conditions too.
Its one of those games you play to death, leave for 6 months and come back to a load of new mods that extend its interest some more.
100 hours entertainment tops. For 15 quid, cant moan though!

Craziest take on Batman I've seen. You think they're just taking you through the motions, once again fetishising the Wayne murders for the hundredth time and then, bam, the first of several curveballs you will not see coming. On a technical level, it is still a Telltale game. Animations are finally starting to improve but the engine still stutters like crazy, even on an overkill PC. Randomly kicks you back to mouse and keyboard prompts while using a gamepad, too.

My review for Half-Life can be seen here:
I like to call this game Half-Life: But S.h.i.t.
Whats this? A NEGATIVE Half-Life game review? Best to downvote it and not read it. As long as something has Half-Life in the title it can't POSSIBLY be♥♥♥♥♥♥ No. Boring at best and flat out bad at worst Blue Shift has the honor of being Half-Life's red headed step child (No offense to red headed step children.). Many will assume that because it's related to Half-Life it's good or that because it's a expansion much like Opposing Force which is considered to be one of the best expansions ever made. Opposing Force was pretty damn good as far as expansions go so this being the Yang to Opposing Forces Yin is disappointing.
If Half-Life were The Terminator and Opposing Force was Terminator 2 then Blue Shift would best be decribed as Terminator 3. Blue Shift came 4 years after Half-Life and 3 years after Opposing Force. Very little has been done and a lot has been taken away or miserably mimicked from the prior titles with the only worthwhile thing to come from this other than an HD model pack was that now one of the many Barney's has been given the last name Calhoun meaning that THIS of all things is canon.
First the positive. The best thing about Blue Shift is it's built upon Gold Source (Really stretching here). While the places you fight the HECU are the highlight of the game because they are ONLY fun thing in the whole game and even then these areas are poorly designed as their placement is poor/careless/haphazard. The HD pack is also a good option to toggle between having on or off. And it's short (A blessing and a curse all considered). I guess it does try something new in regards to having constant interaction with a single NPC named Dr.Rosethal (or something) later in the game but thats about it.
Ho boy onto the bad. Blue Shift feels like someone released an unreleased game that had cancelled early in development with nothing but it's basic skeleton finished, waiting for the meat and muscle to be added prior to the afformentioned cancellation. Released in 2001 and yet free mods have larger more impressivley designed areas, setpeices and scripted sequences for free. It has dull puzzles, and uninteresting story that says nothing new, the game is short yet has a lot of it's lenght taken by REALLY bad Xen levels, and it has lengthy PAINFUL sewer levels early on that very few of my friends have ever even gotten the motivation to get past to this day. It's worst offense is how it fails the core attraction and appeal of Half-Life which is to feel like you have been put into a real/tangible location. Thanks to how bad and bizzare the layouts are past the short opening before the elevator this is failed epicly. Nothing interesting happens. Funnily enough this is far from the worst FPS I've ever played (Chaser and Medal of Honor: Underground for the GBA come to mind.) as it is at least stable/functional but it makes the cardinal sin of wasting my time and being so boring as to make you question why you bothered playing it or games in general.
"How could something made by Valve be bad?" you say. Opposing Force and But S h i t were made by Gearbox in addition to an often forgotten COOP addon for a PS2 port of Half-Life that was worked on by Gearbox. I don't dislike it because it's by Gearbox as that would be petty but if you are inclined to defend it for the glory of Valve as opposed to based on his own merits than at least you know it wasn't by them now. Another annoyance is that Barney goes into space aka Xen without any sort of protective gear so who needs a space suit when you can hold your breath right? They weren't kidding when they said the fabric in their dress shirts can really breath.
Opposing Force is one of the few expansions that was not only great but could stand on it's own so may so maybe the expectations for Blue Shift aren't fair. While Opposing Force is non canon dissapointingly all thanks to it's inclusion of badly designed aliens called Race X Blue Shift on the other hand is. That might be because it has no new weapons or aliens though because it's not like anything interesting happens in Blue Shift other than Barney physically escaping before all the interesting♥♥♥♥♥♥like the military pulling out could happen (Oh and Shepard gets mentioned for some reason in addition to you watching Gordon get dragged away). Considering the time and location Shepard arrived at Black Mesa it's not to hard to believe that there may be weapons Gordon didn't find as the HECU related weapons that Shepard would come across weren't very common compared to the MP5/M4. No new weapons is sort of excusable having played future titles like Half-Life 2: Episode 1 and 2 but considering Opposing Force was probably made by similar people it's ridiculous that they learned nothing and that there was no variety.
No Race X? Thats fine. The Race X aliens didn't fit in with Half-Life's aliens and weren't even fun to fight. In Blue Shift the environments were made small for console in addition to already being painfully linear, uninteresting and looking really out of place. They are REALLY flat. You have sewers, parking lots, sewers, storage rooms, parking lots, sewers, parking lots and Xen. That's a lot of variety ey? All the puzzles take forever and the peices for them move slow as hell. The combat encounters are also a  bore and primarily take place in these afformentioned parking lots or a train yard which while outdoors don't seem to be part of the facility thanks to poor cohesion.
I don't swear often but I must to get to the point and be brash. You are a security gaurd. In Black Mesa. And luckily you are Barney Calhoun out of all of them. Yeah not much is going to happen this should be pretty grounded. Then again this is Black Mesa. Other then the arbitrary showing Black Mesa go to hell during the resonance cascade whats there to show? How many dull ♥♥♥♥ing puzzles can one gaurd survive? I like puzzles so why is this game so bad at them? Where the ♥♥♥♥ are other friendly NPCs and security gaurds after the resonance cascade? You'll see one get killed by zombies and another thrown in a pit but thats all I can recall. Why doesn't Barney talk? Does Black Mesa go out of their way to diversity hire tons of mutes? The amount of mutes around here is getting out of control. Not only that but if it's canon why is Barney so quiet? If Barney spoke that would really give it some personality.
Also I get Barneys resourceful but without the HEV suit or some protective gear he should look like swiss cheese considering all the♥♥♥♥♥♥he survives. In Opposing Force you take more damage because a vest and some armor isn't as protective as an HEV suit but here in Blue Shift they treat nothing but a vest and a dress shirt like a bomb defuesal kit armor wise. Again, the story on offer is just so meaningless and worse yet the gameplay is hampered by the awful design. The fact it's version of Xen managed to be WORSE than Xen in Half-Life is amazing. Not to mention he goes to space with nothing but what you see him wearing on the cover. Stay away and buy Opposing Force or Half-Life if you haven't already!

The atmosphere is enjoyable and the notes you will find sparse through the level contribute to create an eerie ambient and make the exploration a captivating experience, albeit short. The visuals are not bad, but the developers failed to harness the power of the engine making the game unjustifiably heavy and demanding for the graphical quality it has. Many of the models have a too low polygonal count compared to the rest of the assets, same for the textures, some are decent, others are a bit on the low side, and lastly the lighting has some issues, proving distracting from the atmosphere. The sound is again decent, but the music lacks variety, and ends up being repetitive.
The little gameplay it has is mediocre, it doesn't have crippling problems but has some minor issues with dropping and picking up torches and slightly inaccurate hitboxes, and especially unlikable are the bow mechanics and how the main character suddenly interrupts the aiming when the enemy is getting close, making it look more like a glitch than a feature at first. Limiting the character to just exploring and hiding without the ability to use a weapon would have been a better choice, especially since the monster will die with a single arrow to the head and getting hit by the enemy will just respawn the protagonist shortly before the encounters take place, giving the player ample possibility to just keep trying until he succeeds, also eliminating any kind of tension that is crucial to this kind of games.
Also, if you use an average ADSL connection the download will last longer than the game.

This game was kickstarted by a small Canadian company and provides periodic updates and communicates with its player-base quite reguarly. By the time that I am writing this, they have announced a story mode (look up the trailer on youtube) that looks incredibly promising. Though this game is still in Alpha, I have yet to encounter any bugs whatsoever.
TL;DR: Incredibly engaging game that is very rewarding to play, is easy to run, has no bugs, has great devs and extremely fun.

I'm not sure why there are so many positive reviews for this game, because I gave it way more of a chance than I would normally for such a lackluster game.
The graphics are taxing on my hardware, despite them being at their lowest.  (for reference I can run Planetside 2 at 35FPS with this rig.)  That is beside the point though.  There is a game here, where you can go almost anywhere you'd go in a normal casino, and you get 250 free chips every 15 minutes.  The theory is solid, but the execution is inevitably boring.
Walking around with 400,000 chips from my slot jackpot, I found that there was absolutely no way to splurge my money.  I played literally every game in the casino 20 or so times and still couldn't throw away my money.  That's not a bad thing, but normally in my situation, a player would be having major fun. I was in the battlefield, proudly serving the Third Reich, defending our rightfully earned teritory from the Russian dogs. I was killing Russian after Russian, with Das Deutschlandlied blaring in the background. A Russian peeks his head out of the trench in front of me, and stares me down. I stare at him back, and he ducks. I toss my Stick of Germany Glory, or what you like the call a 'grenade' in the trench, and he pops back out and shoots me. I lie there, dying, but a smile on my face. I look at him one last time, and utter my last words, "All hail Deutschland." He blows up, body in the air, and I lie there in glory of the battlefield.
EDIT: Might as well make this a real review.
So first off, I got this game since a couple of my friends played this so I thought "Why not, let's see why     they love this so much." This is no regular, main stream WWII game just like Call of Duty. If you're looking for a game like that, just walk away man. Just walk away. Red Orchestra 2 features a game mode, popular by the community, called Territory/Realism. It's basically a campaign between the Axis (Nazis) and Allies (Red Army/Russians) where you fight for territories across Russia into Stalingrad, hence the name, Heroes of Stalingrad. The realism part is self explanitory. Bullet drop, one shot kills (with bolt action rifles), etc. I always play this mode whenever I'm on, although, a lot of good servers for Terrioty/Realism are full, it's worth finding a good match. This also includes Rising Storm, which is basically the same thing except it's in the Pacific, where it's Japanese vs United States. Offering new maps, it also gives a larger variety of weapons. The United States are given the flamethrower (or as I prefer to call it by its origional German name, fammenwafer). I don't really need to explain that, do I? The Japanese Squad Leaders and Team Leaders spawn with a katana. That's right, a ♥♥♥♥ing katana. With that, they could 'bonzai', which is charging the enemy head on, katana out and ready to kill some dishonerabu Americans (just a joke... don't get butthurt) and now has pretty much became the official Japanese tactic against Americans.
TL;DR ---  In all honesty, I ♥♥♥♥ing love this game. If you want a challenging, realistic WWII game, this is for you.

I had a strong playthrough once. I made it to around day twenty, having gone through three of the available areas at the time, and I was doing good, but it was not long lived. My resources were dwindling as I made my way to the last supplied area at the top of a mountain, a lone radio station secluded from the rest of the map. It was starting to get dark, and my body temperture was dropping fast, so I lit my lantern and started to run. Out in the darkness I heard a howl, followed by another that seemed much closer. I put away my lantern and took out my rifle, aiming it towards the origin of the noise. I heard a growl about ten feet away, so I fired a shot. A whimper pierced the whirring of the cold winter air around me, then silence. Not taking any chances, I lit a flare to see what was around me. Five feet in front of me was a pair of wolves, one was bleeding profusely from his gunshot wound, while the other was preparing to leap onto its would be prey. Being only fifty feet from the radio station, I decided to make a break for it. I threw the flare at the wolves face and sprinted away. The rapid stomping of my feet began to slow as my stamina quickly depleted. No heat for miles takes a toll on the body, and I was slowly dying just feet from my salvation. I heard fast taps on the ground behind me as the wolves closed in for the attack. I was almost there, just a few more steps until I could get into the station and shut the door, then the wolf pounced. I was on the ground, hacking it apart with my axe as it took gnawed on my half frozen flesh. It was a bite away from ending my long journey, when I took one last swing with my hatchet and killed it. I got up and limped toward the door, just barely making it into the station before the other wolf had a chance at killing me. I made it. Inside was much needed health supplies, and much needed food. I started a fire and cooked some venison, all the while warming my body temperture to its original state. I then went to sleep in the nearby cot, gaining health, yet also gaining thirst and hunger. My supplies were low, maybe a few energy bars and a few cans of soda, definitely not enough to last a voyage out into the unknown, so I decided that my journey had come to an end. I quit the game and said goodbye, for I knew that if I continued I would surely perish. I couldn't watch my character die, after all we had been through, he didn't deserve to fade into the long dark. So I let him live in that save, untouched and undying, until I decide that it's time for his journey to come to a close. Until that moment, I will always cherish my adventure I had, and I hope that one day I will have the courage to once more venture out into the unknown, making my way through the barren landscape, and surviving the long dark.

Gameplay:
I revealed about 40% of my map maybe 45% found the Dawn Machine traveled far North lost half my crew to madness and the elements; threw a dozen of the living dead overboard after stealing their money for fare (hey at least we didn't eat them, yet) found a stowaway, fought a moustached creature who made fun of my lack of class, ate his still sighing innards, found pearls? Pros:
Story events are varied and intriguing
Making echos the in-game currency is easy with a trade route
Turning your lights off to float past pirates makes you feel like a swampy James Bond
Turning around to put your boot to their butt crack makes you feel like BA Baracus on uber-roids.
Romances are fun, and usually lead to things you can pass down or more interesting stories. Haven't run into any that were gender-locked or species locked? As it were?
Cons:
Not going to keep your attention if this isn't the kind of game you enjoy.
Misleading videos, the game is a novel with the occasional choose your own adventure that ends in peril or horrific peril, very rarely a trinket of worth.
Stats mean too much early-mid game, when you are finding things but your stats keep you from exploring anything of note.
Ships you need to make large sums of echoes, cost even larger sums of echoes lol
Your first ship will cost more than your first cozy lodging
The music is very atmospheric but you only hear it every now and again
DLC isn't on sale with the base game, which means most people won't buy either waiting for a reduction in both not just one. (this may not be their choice) but the DLC is supposedly extraordinary doesn't make sense to only drop one for a large reduction.
Final thoughts:
From the beginning (literally) the screens you create your captain with, are the screens you'll be staring at most of the game, think of it as a mildly interactive graphic novel. Yes you can find more twists and turns than a duck's wang but will you? Verdict:
Would only buy if you're interested in the genre of game, try their web-based game for a tour of the atmosphere/gamesetting if you're still on the fence.

I’m not going to sugar-coat it; this is a walking simulator. If you don’t like walking simulators, you aren’t going to like this. If you are looking for a game, you aren’t going to like this. I caught a lucky break in being able to play this game while it was free to play for a previous weekend. Once the right funds were freed up, I bought this game without hesitation and have not regretted it since.
A bit of fair warning is in order. The game is anything but fair in what obstacles and monsters it throws at you before you're ready to take it on (which makes it a bit like Dark Souls, with the difference being that running is a perfectly valid and sane option). The UI, particularly objectives, are a mess to sort through, at least in the beginning. You'll be spending a good deal of the game trying to figure out home waters locations that too many people seem to expect you to know right off the bat (and which you will have to discover on your own). And yet, if you are willing to overlook these things, Sunless Sea can be a truly rewarding experience.
What I love the most about the game is how it is the only game I've ever encountered that is a purely post-Lovecraftian apocalypse universe. The world of the Unterzee is one where the Great Old Ones have come and (largely) gone. All that's left are the unfortunate human survivors of Fallen London, surrounded by alien beings and creatures in an equally alien environment. Finding out more about this world is the key appeal to playing it. Even as you start sweating how much fuel and supplies you've got to make it to the next port or how thin your hull's gotten and, OMG, is that a massive zee-monster over there, unraveling this world's mysteries through exploration makes it all worthwhile. And that's not even getting into the various officers that you can have on your ship, all of whom have their own crazy quirks and stories to tell...
I'm actually something of a fan of the game's combat, as frustrating as it sometimes can be. It reminds of a fantasy version of the old Sid Meir's game Pirates!, which had a similar system in place. The line of sight mechanics offered by the lamp system gives it a bit of a challenge to make it worth your while. Still, I'll probably have to wait until I upgrade to something better than my starter ship before I can actually call it "fun". A tip for combat novices: hug any enemy ships you encounter as closely as possible, away from the light. You'll need to adjust your speed constantly to make this work. But when you do, you'll find yourself sinking ships with three times your hull strength in a decent amount of time.
All in all, I want more of this game and look forward to trying out its DLC Zubmariner. This is one real-time strategy/exploration game that has a very unique concept and execution.

Outlast....... it's just as much as my heart could handle. I bought this game after it has been on the market for years. I watched youtube gameplays from pewdiepie a lot and should know where the game would take me to when i bought it. But still when I played the game, the thrill, the horror, the scares were still fresh, always fresh actually.
I have never experienced such awesomeness in any horror game, not even close to "not a lot". For Red Barrels to actually make something new and revolutionary, it deserves a hundred percent positive review.
Now for the start, the gameplay of this game is pretty simple. it's just run, hide, or die game. Simply no puzzle, no mini games in the game, not an open world but there are parts where you are in a maze and the game forces the pursuer to pursue You. Another challenge is, you have choices that you will make for yourself, you want to be paranoic and scared by every single person in the game, or be selective and brave, or be consumed by murderous curiousity. This is one of the first things that you will then feel throughout the game. Others might find the game a little funny, but for me, those guys might have problems, I personally consider this game a nightmare.
However, this game has the charm that makes the player want to touch that shortcut to hell again and again, and again they meet hell. This curiousity that they trap you in, is something that you cannot avoid after you buy the game.
After finishing the whole game (including the DLC). I found the enemies not scary anymore (their physical appearance) and the game does not give you nightmares in real life. It's just the tension you get when you dont want the bad guys to find and kill you, or get you when they chase you. This is the charm of the game. So don't be scared of buying it, or emptying your wallets. I really reccommend you to play this! Enjoy your nightmare!

Audiosurf is an interesting and unique game in the modern space of rhythm games, but features a variety of problems due to quanitity over quality. There are a variety of game modes to play with and the basic of gameplay in each mode involves touching colourful blocks that are calibrated to the beats in a song you choose. There is a core problem with this however, as unless you use incredibly basic music notes can be off, a sin for a rhythm game. Many of the modes focus on collecting certain colourful blocks for maximum score, meaning that you will hit notes in a strange way. Although of these major flaws due to procedual generated maps it makes up for it is style - the track travels fast, during intense moments in songs, twisting and turning red, while during slowler moments in travels upwards with cool colours.
TL;DR: Being procedually generation has its perks as you can use any sound file on your computer compared to traditional rhythm games that limit your track selection to preselected songs, but be aware that more often then not notes can be off. This game is more focuses on getting a high score, which can involve missing beats in a song which can be jarring.

Alpha Review:
Evolve is a 4v1 Hunter .VS. Monster game where both sides can literally demolish each other. At first, it may seem like hope is lost as the monster but as you 'Evolve' and put your points into abilities you become a real terror to the hunters if used correctly, the time I played was mostly as a Trapper or Monster, both of which I can say were amazing. Being able to decimate a group of hunters as the Monster was extremely satisfying after all that feeding and evolving. On another side, being able to work with my team and take down this monstrosity before it killed us was exhilarating. The start of the Alpha wasn't super great but hey, it's an alpha, what do you expect? After the devs quickly fixed the issue which in my eyes was nice. They immediately sprung to action to fix it, that's quality dev work to me.
The four classes you can pick from are as follows;
Medic: Basic healing class that has a slow for the monster
Trapper: Pretty much a support class that traps the monster with Harpoons and the Mobile Arena
Assault: Basic tanking class comes w/ a shield and tripmines for extra damage.
Support: Literally as the name suggests. Support the tank by providing a shield or help out a teammate getting pummeled by that monster and shield them and there's also the orbital barrage which unleashes a devastating orbital bombardment on the monster.
The three maps that were available were nice as well and didn't really feel similar at all. Some monsters did but overall the layout was nice and different each time.
Now for the progression system, I don't normally play survival-shooters like this with a progression system to unlock characters but it felt challenging and simple. "Get so many kills with this to partially unlock the big unlock" That's a nice simple way to put it, it gave me a sense of satisfaction when I finally earned the character/elite skin.
The bonus' you can get too helped when you were playing certain classes. Want to track an enemy as a trapper? Movement speed increase is your best friend. Need more damage? Better grab that damage output.
Overall, I'd definitely replay this game with my friends and would even be willing to buy it. On a scale of 1-10, it'd definitely go for about a 8 at it's current state.

There are lot of reviews out there that would recommend this game but have a lot of negative things to say and I feel like most are unbalanced, so I hope this is a bit more balanced.
First, if you aren't familiar with the Telltale style this game is going to seem low quality, but let's be honest here. It's a $25 game for a reason! This was never ment to compete with the Arkham series, it was never designed to be a large game in that way. I finished it in 9 hours one day. Graphically it's not top quality, nor was it ment to be. If you're interested in this game, know what you're getting into! This is a game about characters and choices.  Some reviews are going to tell you there are no real consequences for your choices and that isn't true because the consequences come from how the people around you percieve you. If that isn't enough for you this isn't the game for you, and that's ok! But please don't come into this game expecting something it was never ment to be. This game is designed to make you feel like Batman/Bruce Wayne while at the same time delievering a story and consistent game experience. Things do change as you make choices, and yes, most of those changes come from the characters not the story arc, so be aware.
Overall, most people will likely play it once through unless they want to see alternative choices or want to correct a "mistake", but remember, for the price point and the way it was designed, 30 bucks for a 9 hour fun experience isn't to bad in my book. There are bowling alley's that charge more.

*THIS IS AN ALPHA REVIEW*
*TL;DR VERSION AT BOTTOM*
Day 1: Super hyped, started game with 2 other friends only to find that the matchmaking was busted. Fell back on some other games for a few hours in which the devs fixed the issue.
- Having a medium gaming rig caused stuttering on lowest of low setting, but nothing ground breaking. Couldn't appreciate graphical fidelity, but it wasn't anything I care much about nowadays
- Hunting a monster felt satisfying, after a few rounds one REALLY gets into the spirit of things and it becomes a thrill. To date no game felt for me this way.
Day 2: Game was running okay, decided to try out monster.
- Heart pounding and super stressed while playing. The hunters never let up and a player could really feel like a beast being chased and cornered. To date, no game made me so breathless and on the edge of my seat.
- Reaching level 3 and pounding hunters to bits felt satisfying after all the stress of avoiding them. The game rewards you immensely if you play it right as monster.
- Subsequently, next monster game I got rekt. Didn't feel bad about it because the hunters were really good and organised.
- Playing with friends again, we had a few epic matches and last stands, enough stories to go talk our gamer friends' ears off. Granted some monsters were clueless and lost within minutes, but those that avoided us for more than 10 minutes were an enjoyable hunt.
Day 3:
- By this time we could be considered fairly proficient in the game. Tactics were developed to better follow and trap the beast, where to defend and how to corral the critter into a more favourable location.
- Watched friend play the monster, and there are a lot of things the bugger can do to make the game more exciting. Hunters, ALWAYS CHECK YOUR BUSHES! Seriously, it makes you less embarrassed when you watch the replays afterwards.
- Kraken is glass canon and must be trapped in a cave. *shrugs*
-= TL;DR VERSION =-
- Devs are really working hard on the game and are fair to players (The Alpha got extended due to problems on the PS4 for all platforms, yay!)
- Playing as hunters, cooperation is critical, so you're better off playing with friends. The game isn't as fun if you don't communicate.
- Playing monster is super difficult and you should first play hunter and observe. When played right, you are allowed to feel like a stealthy badass.
- Even for an Alpha, this game is pretty much finished. I have confidence that by release it will be a must-buy for me.
- Some may say that the game loses it's replayability after a few matches. If you play with friends and against skilled foes, I guarantee that won't be the case.

I'll add my opinion to this game for anyone who cares.  Batman - The Telltale Series (Children of Arkham) is an original story on the Batman mythos.  For that, you shouldn't expect a Batman origin tale, nor a hardened Batman of experience tale either.  Imagine Batman: Year One as a start point, and you'll have a sense of where this is going.  The game is pretty much the driver in this road trip, and you're just the passenger, giving some directions to the destination.  The outcome of the story will more or less be the same, but the actions you take will influence some things here or there.
If you are a Batman fan who enjoys the idea that each alternate Batman tale gives credence to DC Comic's multiverse idea, then you'll have no problem with variations on villan introductions, obscure relationships amongst characters, and alterations to established minor characters.  If you're someone who thinks that the only established canon of batman came from Bob Kane's Batman Returns (nevermind the Batman of the 30's or 60's, etc) then this game won't sit too well with you.
The music and voice acting are quite good - I didn't expect Shakepeare or something from Game of Thrones, and the responses are decent enough to make you feel concerned about what you say to whom.  Being a jerk to Alfred, Selina, Harvey or Gordon really makes you feel terrible for being a jerk, but the option is always there.
The game itself seeks to humanize Bruce Wayne as Bruce Wayne, as well as Batman, but what you decide is how the story is tailored.
There are moments where I was left wondering how to solve puzzles or make connections on how certain things relate to other.  The detective work in the game felt a little clunky, and trying to figure out why something didn't match with another was a little annoying.  These moments didn't make the game shine, and really should get reworked prior to the next series coming out.
The story, however, was engaging, and I felt like I really wanted to get to the next chapter.  The pace is a little slow, and in the hour or two I would spend playing the game in my free time, I progressed further in plots with my Batman comics.
In the end, I would recommend this game to you with the advice that comparing it to anything you know of Batman is simply seeking to not enjoy the game on its own merits.  This game was quite enjoyable, and TellTale should work on building the good points of this game in the next series, and cut out the annoying parts.

Edge of Space recently came out of Early Aceess, can i just start off by saying that this is a brilliant start. In an industry where developers leave their game to die with no content and sparawling fans: "cough, cough" DayZ.
Edge of space is a 2D, Openworld Adventure game. The main story goes like this, You were in cryogenic sleep when your ship broke down, so you wake up and you go exploring the planet beneith you for recourses, not too shabby for a starting story. The story continues with a character named Rufus who is an interesting character to say the least. I wont spoil any more but i doubt you were looking at this game for its story. You want to know about the gameplay, the exploration. Well im glad to say that it's awsome. The game has many simularities to Terraria and Starbound but it improves on these things and adds more to them. For example in Terraria you have your ranks of gear going from a wooden sword to a Gold sword going to a Lights Bane. In Edge of Space, you have sooo many more options mainly because you have to earn xp to unlock new items which is awsome because you dont grind xp by killing mobs (well you can but there is a more enjoyable way to do it) you get xp for mining ore and it basically rewards you for exploring. You will also encounter these things called "nests" which you can explore and destroy for even more xp, which is cool. You also have your character skill trees, but when i say skill trees i dont mean like the stealth, the tank ect. I mean you specialise in what your doing. For example i could get builders armour, if i was interested in building stuff in the game, this would neglect the mob damage and illiminate annoyances that might stop you from building.
There is a large range of things to makr that you actually want to get unlike other games where they have you craft random crap just so you can continue with the story, Edge of space doesnt do that, instead they let you build mechs, pets, new weapons and badass jetpacks. These arnt just useless vanity items they do infact effect the way you play and make it more enjoyable.
So far im loving this game too pieces, being a big fan of Terraria and Starbound helped i guess, but i'd honestly reccomend it to anyone who loves open world exploration games as there is stuff to find and tonnes of things to make, there is no doubt a wealth of content here.....which is really great! :)

This game, is an absolutely amazing game. It is set in and around Stalingrad, where the Germans and the Russians face off for victory. It is also set in and around the South-East Asian-Pacific region, where the Japanese and the Americans face off for victory. It is brutally realistic and gritty. A bullet from most weapons to the torso will kill you most of the time, same to the kneck or head. To the arms or legs most of the time it will wound you. Even if you are not killed after being wounded, if the wound is anywhere other than your limbs, you must patch yourself fast or you will bleed out, just like in reality. If it is in your limbs you may or may not bleed out, sometimes you have to judge if its better to run to cover and then heal, or heal on the spot and hope you don't get shot again. Or maybe you don't need to heal at all and you can save your bandages for worse wounds. The weapons have realistic recoil, and clear advantages and disadvantages for all situations. The Germans favor medium to long range fighting, the Russians medium to short range. The Germans and Russians are both perfectly capable of attacking and defending, but the Germans have an edge when it comes to attacking due to having longer ranged weapons, the only assault rifle in the world at the time, and machine guns with very high rates of fire that are very good for pinning the enemy down. The Russians have an edge on defense due to being good at letting the enemy come to them and grinding them down in close quarters fighting, along with the superior PPSH 41 sub machine gun, and superior mosin nagant bolt action rifle with its amazing accuracy that can blow the enemy away at close range even with sloppy aiming. Basically, some weapons for one side are superior to the other's equivalent. The audio in this game is stunning and extremely intense, much better than other shooters. This game is also extremely reliant on team work, no one-man armies allowed. If one team is communicating and working together, and the other is not, then the team that is working together will crush the other one. If both are doing what they are supposed to be doing then you get incredibly intense matches.
The Rising Storm side of the game is pretty different from the Stalingrad part, for example Asymmetric warfare plays a huge role. The Japanese cannot face off against the Americans head on in open areas, the Americans just have too much fire power. The Japanese need to utilize the environment to keep mobility over the enemy and to take cover, jungle fighting is where they excell. All of the American riflemen have semi-automatic rifles, something neither the Japanese, nor the Germans or Russians get to have for their riflemen, and riflemen make up the bulk of the team. All of the other American classes have gear with superior raw damage and rates of fire to that of the Japanese, but what the Japanese excell at is their ferocity, combined with ingenious things such as creating frag grenade booby traps, knowing when to keep their distance so as to pick the enemy off from long range with their more accurate and longer range bolt action rifles, their knee mortars, and banzai charging in a small area in a big spearhead with smoke grenades and mortar/artillery/naval barrage support. The Japanese are definitely more geared towards attacking so as to hit the Americans on their terms and to overwhelm them in massed attacks, whereas the Americans, due to their superior raw fire power, are best on defense because they can dig in and if the Japanese run around in open areas they can mow them down like German machine guns on D-Day (Saving private Ryan style)
And speaking of D-Day, there is currently a 1944-1945 US vs German mod in development with testing events every few days, which will be like a fan made expansion which will bring the game up to 3 different theaters.
And on top of that a World War I mod is in the early stages of development with both western and eastern front gameplay.
There are no hackers whatso ever, there are some modded maps that are optional to play on, and the vast majority of the player base are cool people, who don't mess around, are not casual, and who play to win, all of which creates an extremely intense gaming experiance.
This game is one of the best games I have ever played, and I HIGHLY recommend it to everyone.
It's way better than what Call of Duty and Battlefield have turned into.

A lot of people have mentioned that it's a bit tough getting into the game at the start, and I would have to agree with that. Fineous's dialogue options help, but it can be really difficult deciding where to spend those first precious Science points.
My best tip: upgrade your jetpack (fighter, explorer, or builder) and make a better primary weapon (phase or melee) first! Having an upgraded jetpack makes a huge difference to mobility, and the starter weapon really seems to only be there to get you used to crafting -- by making you craft a better one.
All in all, I'm having a lot of fun. Thanks for the game and congratulations on release!

Cautious Recommendation.
I waited till post launch to play this game as it was something both me and my bf were looking at since we enjoyed terraria so much. So I will go through a few pros and cons from my experience thus far.
Pros
- Gameplay is fun when playing with multiple people, there are features such as resurrecting dead players that you will miss out in if you play singleplayer.
- Questing is quick and easy normally. It can be a bit grindy for some of the quests but the rewards seem to usually be worth it. It instills a sense of progression that is enjoyable to experience.
- The details on your character armor and progression trees that allow you different armor if you play a certain style give a unique vibe and add potential replayability.
- Knowledge skill trees give you lots of ways to specialize as you progress in early game and it is especially helpful if you have multiple players with you, letting you all specialize in different ways and combine your knowledge to progress quicker.
Cons
- Do not try to exit game and try to get back if you are running a server. The steam client will not allow you to start game back up till you take your server down. This is also a huge problem if you crash or have any gamebreaking bugs.
-
Issue fixed as of sept 19th hotfix.
- Exploding monster nests can leave the sound of bomb alarms going off long after its been destroyed, making an annoying sound that just wont disapear.
- Monster ai leaves a  lot to be desired.
- Building seems to take a while to make anything worthwhile and there is not as much a need to build actual homes like other games in this genre.
- It is incredibly challenging to figure out how to get many types of building materials, leading to constant searching of wiki to figure out how to find many types of materials.
- Certain materials that were used in many types of items were incredibly rare to find, making it so that more people you had with you, the more challenging and difficult it was to even find enough materials to get everyone basic items.
Overall, I would recommend waiting on this game for a few more patches or unless you like what you see. The game is enjoyable but there is quite a few issues with it that can lessen the enjoyment in both singleplayer and multiplayer post launch.

Outlast....... it's just as much as my heart could handle. I bought this game after it has been on the market for years. Now for the start, the gameplay of this game is pretty simple. it's just run, hide, or die game. Simply no puzzle, no mini games in the game, not an open world but there are parts where you are in a maze and the game forces the pursuer to pursue You. Another challenge is, you have choices that you will make for yourself, you want to be paranoic and scared by every single person in the game, or be selective and brave, or be consumed by murderous curiousity. This is one of the first things that you will then feel throughout the game. Others might find the game a little funny, but for me, those guys might have problems, I personally consider this game a nightmare.

Like many people who voted negative to this before me and devoted more time to it, you will like this game if you belong to a particular niche of individual.
I for one am not in that camp.
My problem is that this game suffers HORRIBLY from the "are you showing us the most exciting times of your character's life? No? Why the hell not?" series of questions. In short, the spaces between islands is traversed paralyzingly slowly for a game that has nothing to fidget with in between trips. You can literally just trawl along, waiting, praying in vain for an event. A fight. Something. Anything. It's kind of meta in the madness it instills. Even the fights are tacked on at best, unmitigated garbage at worst.
I did have a bit of fun with it for a time once I got a slightly faster ship, but the problem with a faster, possibly lighter ship is that you need more crew. With more crew, you need more food. With more food, you need more money. With a lack of money, death is more frequent. So a faster ship becomes a moot point. So the more able you become in exploration and fun-having, the more likely you are to perish and get sent back to the doldrums. You do get to give your progeny an asset as inheritance but I did this several times after reaching early end-game and NEVER got anything that mitigated the staggering boredom of the early game.
I would find this game much more enjoyable if all ships had a 1.5x base speed modifier OR something to meaningfully kill time while cruising. Because any game where I spend the vast majority of the time READING A BOOK WHILE I WAIT IS NOT A GOOD GAME. And I can't even do that because I have to watch the light levels around my ship so my people don't go ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ from the encroaching darkness. So it's a game that forces me to pay attention with a single innocuous action that I have to devote all my attention to if I want to live when I could be doing more productive things.
It is for this alone that I condemn Sunless Sea to a games oubliette, because the stories are not actually bad at all. They simply aren't enough to redeem its tortured soul.
Maybe Sunless Skies will be better. Unless they bring us slow space zeppelins or some ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥.

So, I had the pleasure of pouring fourteen hours into this game in one sitting, because it was a Sunday and there is obviously little else to do when you are the only human being within a fifty mile radius. So... review time.
Game was in its Alpha stage, but for an Alpha game, it performed fairly well and met expectations I had put forth. Coming into contact with the Monster as a Hunter is both intense and a little bit frightening at times. Most Monsters were not talented enough to take advantage of many of the awesome features for hiding that they had, but I did manage to hide in a bush as one was coming towards me and jumped him for a sneak attack that freaked him out so bad he almost♥♥♥♥♥♥his pants.
'Nuff on that.
There's four classes with two variants of each, thus far, the medic, the support, the assault, and the trapper. Each plays a differently role and for the most part, the synergy between classes is rather nice. At the current time, there were two different monsters to choose from: the behomoth and the kraken, of which the kraken was far more OP and probably could use a tad bit of balance.
The general flow of gameplay has three stages based upon the Monster's current level of evolution, hence the name of the game. At stage one, the monster typically is disadvantaged, unless they are the Kraken in which case they can still wipe an overconfident team with little trouble. Stage two puts the two forces on relatively even footing and combat could go either way. Stage three generally ends the game in one way or the other unless the Monster had a rough early game, because at this point it is powerful enough to basically steamroll the hunters.
At the current time, they are asking 60$ for pre-order, but from the lack of diverse content (during the alpha) Id say that is not quite worth it, especially since there are very few pre-order bonuses that you wont unlock within the first few hours of play. That being said, they are intending to add more monsters and maps and game modes, so by the time it hits full release, it might be worth it.
While I recommend the game, I also recommend holding off on it unless you /really/ want it or want to support the Devs, which probably don't need a lot of monetary support, but that's up to you to decide.

In summary, the game is a borefest with a casino skin.  If you like sitting around pretending to play poker and blackjack, then this game might be for you.  But if you are a normal human being who enjoys mental stimulation... Steer clear of this waste of time.

First of all, let me just say that
is not the typical game I play. Nevertheless, as I was impressed by FTL for a while and seeing the generous free weekend offer by Failbetter Games, I decided to sample this popular story driven title. I'll try and keep this review brief, so here's my personal take on Sunless Sea after about 10hrs of on/off-line gameplay on my laptop over the weekend:
Pros:
+ Compelling story, with many secrets to be discovered; persistent storyline even after loss of the captain (next captain inherits some stats)
+ Great atmosphere, with a touch on the creepy side
+ Randomised zee map, except for a few story driven places; adds to its longevity
+ Some very funny quests and the ability to romance your officers with unexpected results
Cons:
- Story becomes convoluted after a while, perhaps due to all the side quests.
- The atmosphere was great at first but after ~5hrs gameplay, due to repetitiveness, I found myself mostly skimming through the choices without bothering to read them at length when making port. To survive you really need fuel and supplies, so the rest seem unimportant when your only goal (short term at least) is to explore as much as possible and get paid by the Admiralty (only reliant source of income).
- The graphics and effects are passable, making Sunless Sea rise just a step above a textual MUD adventure (feels like old school RPG).
- Some obvious balance problems, especially at the start, adding to the difficulty of the game (grinding enemies became necessary for my initial survival). After a few perma-deaths, I finally and only by luck managed to get a big payday, which in turn helped with upgrades, making Sunless Sea considerably more fun. Quests hardly make you any money (echoes) and trading is non-existent when you lack funds and have a tiny 40 spaces hold, shared with your supplies and fuel (read a few excellent guides along the way from workshop to progress faster).
- The darkness of the top-down gothic design adds to the atmosphere but after a while it all starts to look the same, port after port (I would have liked to see some more distinct vibrancy represented by different cultural and color map changes).
-----
TL;DR: All in all myself and family quite enjoyed
for what it was, a dark survival exploration adventure with a good story. I would definitely recommend it to all fans of the genre, especially at the heavily discounted price currently going on Steam. In addition a big thumbs up to
for providing us with a free weekend to sample their game and wish more developers would follow suit to their example.

The only thing better than listening to your music, is riding your music while you listen to it.
A novel game at the time of its initial release, Audiosurf is essentially a rhythm-based game, whereby your experience is based on and varies by the music you choose to load into the engine. The track layout and pace are all algorithm dependant and are generated by the song you load in - faster tracks are more intensive, while slow music is relaxing and a cruise. Add in the multiple game modes, and the fun never stops, as long as you are listening to something you enjoy.
Highly recommended to anyone who loves games, and anyone who loves music.

You want some action? Come get some! This sneak peek weekend showed what the game is about and how far they are with the development. Goliath weekend with good 1v4 gaming action.
Basicly its just about an evolving monster engaging on humans and a spec-ops-team trying to get down the monster.
Playing as a monster or as a member of the spec-force, both can be hard to play, depending on the map. The main objective for the monster is to eat little monsters and evolve to get stronger to get down the hunters or the power relay. The Hunters try to kill the monster by chasing it. As the monster is obviously faster then the Hunters they should try to place traps (mines/hooks) at keypoints on the map and lead it into the direction of it. On other maps there is also the opportunity to intercept it. Also monster can climb almost anywhere but  a hunter has to use the jetpack wisely to follow. None should try to face the monster alone. Every hunterclass is inportant for the team to win.
Nice animations of the environment, little monsters and creatures also with a great flora. Didn't saw any major graphic bug. Sometimes if you hit a mine and you were jumping you fly up to the roof of the trees. Couldn't test on highest settings cause of my machine limitation - tested on medium settings with no tessellation.
As a hunter I had problems following the monster cause it was so hilly and the jetpack runs out very fast. Cause I played the Monster very often it was easy just to jump down somewhere and climb up after they followed. They are stucked there then for like 20 seconds - if jetpack is empty.
It's a very team-based game - if you play as a hunter of course. So if there is one weak hunter, that can turn into a losing fight very easily. Arenas are not always "healthy" for the hunters. An overall "meh" game in Telltale's lineup of licensed games with constant stuttering and glitches even after a 9GB update. I made two complete playthroughs of the game before writing this review.
Pros:

- A few detective puzzles here and there gives a fresh take on gameplay where you literally "link" evidences to deduce
events that occur at a crime scene (though it can be too easy and unchallenging)
Cons:
- Combat is nothing but QTEs and overall feel is unsatisfying (it doesn't even matter if you miss the button prompts)
- Too much hand holding makes you feel like a numbskull rather than an actual badass
- Another typical Telltale formula where most choices ultimately don't matter (save for a few in later episodes)
- Glitches and stutters GALORE! Pretty much making the 9GB update pointless
Conclusion:
If you're into storytelling and little else and think that the plot twist in Episode 1 (which is free) is interesting enough, by all means get it but only on SALE.
If you're into games that actually make you feel like you're Batman, go get one of the Arkham games.
If you want a Telltale game where your choices actually matter, get Tales from the Borderlands or Guardians of the Galaxy instead.

Oh Banished... Banished is hands down one of the more realistic city builders out there. Banished takes what we love about a city builder and adds even more to it. The constant monitoring of supplys, resources, trade and general health of your towns folk doesn't even begin to scratch the surface. The AI while impressive is anguishing at times, and yes I mean times of pure frustration followed by cursing and even having to get a beer to calm myself.
Banished is almost detailed to a fault, a good fault but none the less a fault of its own. If you are lucky enough to make it past the first couple of years’ life in your town will continue to have its own unique struggles. My most successful town, now 105 years old, continues to go through its own challenges. Often brought on by my own ignorance or a minor hiccup in city planning. Occasionally you will have an outbreak of the flu or contaminated food but once you achieve a population greater than one hundred or so this really isn’t a problem as the doctor will be able to fix you right up. The greatest two issues every player will undoubtedly face is starvation and your citizens dying of freezing temperatures (lack of firewood). The issue here is while the game is addicting it’s easy to get caught up in the non-essential functions of your town. While having stone roads is great, having food and firewood should always take the gamers attention as an everyday issue.
If the player is lucky enough to get through the troubling times of a village on the brink of extinction early on, fret not the threat is still real with even a population of five hundred plus. I found that allocation of resources is more important than ever in a large population. Perhaps a flaw of the AI used to control these villagers is that they don’t seem to do many things with any rhyme or reason. For example, if I have a large quantity of chicken in one storage shed but that shed is on the other side of the map my towns people with make the journey to find it. Often times by the time they arrive villagers that live closer have grabbed the precious artificial sustenance and have left their fellow man to die. The problem with this is that there is no “F5” for the villager now traveling what is going to take them a seasons time to get the meat that doesn’t exist. They will pass by fully loaded storage facilities as the AI has already populated a destination for them. This is my qualm. Now there are ways around this. Once your town becomes large it’s best to think of every area as its own township in a county. Each area needs its own food supply, its own firewood, its own foresters, harvesters, teachers, doctors and so on. Forgetting this will bring what is all but certain death to the citizens of your village.
My village of five hundred still goes through its random shortages but is generally healthy, most recently I lost over two hundred citizens due to the simple errors mentioned above. All in all this game takes the cake. Its oddly addicting and you almost feel like you are part of this thing that has become great. While you won’t be protecting your city from outside invaders, perhaps the only con I see, you will be the “president” of something great. I’d love to see some updates but overall who can complain? Perhaps we can hope but this is worth every penny you spend. Good luck and have fun being Banished!

In Banished you are controlling a group of Banished people who try to survive in a surrounding field with dangers and opportunities. If you manage well and plan ahead you are rewarded with a thriving town and educated, happy citizens who live their lives in comfort, a price which is quit satisfaction because of the high skill demand of the game. Best explained is the game by saying it is  group survival, real time strategy  and resource management game. A Great thought of and with this game accomplished concept which creates a game that is in some ways the first of its kind. The greatest addition in this game is the "human as resources" element. As in many other RTS games humans are not considered as a strategy giving part at all, like for example in the Anno series. Or the human "resource" management part of the game is not as much advanced as in Banished as for example in the settler series, age of empires series (empire earth series)...  The other great concept of the game is the real time survival strategy part as Banished really feels like a survival game. One mistake and half of your townspeople die in the winter and that's a situation after which it is difficult to recover again.
Banished comes with a huge variety of different and comprehensible resources which are connected with each other in understandable connection and traceable chain productions. For example the hunter does not come home with just meat, he comes home with venison and leather. The venison is than used as food and the leather goes to the tailor to create warmer cloth. Or the gatherer does not just gather food, there are many different roots, mushrooms, berries and herbs it can collect. Its true that the chain productions do not have the advanced level of a Settler 7 or a Anno 1701 but sometimes less is more (or less is not too few).
I personally would have wished for a slower start into the game as one of the first buildings you build in the beginning is a 2 story hunting cabin that than is just filed with one hunter as not enough people are available to hunt. That's a situation which bothered me quit allot as it takes away some parts of the toughly  created realism in the detailed variety of resources.
In general the auto placement of the citizens to houses near to their work side, works good, but a system where the player could decide by himself who is going to live where would have been more intuitive. As it bothered me allot that sometimes the computer would not get it right.
Another situation that totally ruined my first game-round was that I decided its a good idea to build many small farms. Sadly I realized afterwards that managing these farms is an impossible task.
Because each spring it has to be decided which field are work on and what is going to be planed on each field. A selection the player has to make manually by clicking on each field assigning a farmer and selecting the crop. In this situation an automated system would have been an crucial improvement of the game.
In general there is a bad feedback according productivity of all kind of production chains and bad general statistics. A situation that  leaves small room for satisfactory optimizing of the town.
I also think that there is a bit of a balancing problem in late game as it kind of gets more difficult to collect enough timber and stone for upgrading and building higher ranked buildings.
In the conclusion I have to admit that I have a huge respect for the game and its developer as it is a one man project.  I think the comprehensible resources, the general concept of the game and the humans as resources idea is phenomenal but the realization and implementing of some game mechanics is quiet weak.

Short, not scary, and easy.  The character walks too slow, which in my opinion, makes the Medusa's Labyrinth last longer in a cheap way.  Even so, it is less than half an hour of gameplay.  In fact, I'd argue that a really slow character makes death less scary since the player is practically asking to die, and at the same time, the monsters have to be slow along with the player so that the game is playable.  That's my idea.  I'll be honest, I died once, but only because of the poor mobility that I said before, and the poor aim of the bow.  After missing my shot, I looked straight at the monster for a good ten seconds, and said "Well, I'm gonna die."  Then the beast slapped me good, and I picked restart.  The checkpoint was nice.  Oh, I forgot to mention that the monsters initiated an erie ambience when they were close by that got old fast after seeing nothing for five minutes.   If you've played "Among the Sleep" then you know the exact sound, and overuse, that I'm refering to.  Lastly, the game was easy, but not because it was short.  Clearly, the reason being that this was supposed to cause fear throught the atmosphere more than the difficulty, like other horror games, but it fails to do that even when it uses such clear and common noises which aren't chilling at all.
Yes, this was free, but that does not exempt it from criticism, which may actually help future games (and their possible revenue) in the pursuit of the perfect (horror) game.  I didn't think that Medusa's Labyrinth was in the right direction to make a good horror game, and I refuse to believe that many of these reviews would be helping by encouraging others to play a game for the sake of someone's feelings.  Saying "it's not great, but it's free" is not going to make something like Medusa's Labyrinth or its future titles better.  To be clear, I do care about other's feelings, because if I didn't, my review would be one, incomprehendable sentence along the lines of "your dum."

You need to have public opinion on your side in order to get re-elected and keep playing, but if the public turns against you, you have to click on each person to figure out what needs they have personally in order to meet those needs. It would have been better if there was a page that told you exactly what you were lacking in so that you could meet the needs, but I didn't see any, and if any exist then it certainly doesn't come up in the tutorial.

Basically I was left with the impression that there's a lot of things going on in the background and you are not privy to the knowledge without a lot of extra steps. I'm not saying that it's a bad game, but rather that it is not for me. I'll stick to more traditional city-building games.

This game is sequel for original FlatOut, and this game is one god damn good example how to make sequel.
FlatOut was awesome or should i say "perfect" arcade racing game. Though, its from 2004 and still, its kickass game with good driving response system, good and challenging AI, awesome tracks, derby bowls and stunt tracks.
FlatOut 2 have all these same things, but it is made thousand times better!
There is three car classes: Derby class, race class and street class.
Derby cars are cheap and durable and meant for the first class of FlatOut racing. They can take a beating and deliver a powerful punch, but arent as fast as the rest of cars.
Race cars are powerful and they are from competitive price range offer the 'best bang for buck' in the though in second class.
Street cars are tuned up for the most competitive tier of FlatOut racing. Fastest of their kind, but a little less durable.
In total there is 34 cars in game.
Game race tracks are great. you can choose from many different enviroments to race and they are: Forest, Field, Desert, Canal, City and Race. In total there is 30 race tracks in game. There is also 9 special track events in game.
Stunt tracks are also fun to play. There is 12 different stunts to do and they are: High Jump, Bowling, Ski Jump, Curling, Stone-Skipping, Ring Of Fire, Field Goal, Royal Flush, Basketball, Darts, Baseball and Soccer.
Derby bowls is one of the best things in this game. Its all about earning wrecking points by dealing damage, destroying cars and ultimately surviving the challenge.
The ragdoll physics in the sequel have been greatly updated. During the race, the driver may be thrown out of the car if slammed into a wall at a high speed.
AI in this game is fine. You compete with seven bots in race at same time. They are challenging and fun, but they can be sometimes really cocky.
Soundtrack is awesome in this game, it contains rock and metal music from Nickelback, Megadeath, Papa Roach, Mötley crue and many more...

It's Bioshock, what else do I need to say? It's crazy, it's smart, it's intense! The story is amazingly detailed and catching. You play as a man named Jack, who lands in the middle of the ocean, next to a lighthouse after a plane crash. Upon entering it, he gets taken into the underwater-city of Rapture, built by the millionaire Andrew Ryan. After the civil war, the city is not under control of sane people or Ryan himself, but ruled by crazy lunatics and geneticly mutated citizens of Rapture. Luckily you are helped by a man named Atlas, who gives you calls to tell you where to go next and what to do.
In the game, you have an arsenal of weapons and power at your disposal. From wrenches, over shotguns and crossbows, to syringes filled with fluids that give you the abilities to shoot fire or lightning from your fingertips, use telekenesis and take control of other peoples bodies. (Just be careful with those Big Daddys!) These so called 'Plasmids' are what make Bioshock a unique shooter with an amazing story and characters, that catch you from start to finish.
I highly recommend any Bioshock game to everyone who likes non-linear shooters, which are different from the rest.

I bought the game when it was on Greenlight a while back, and while it has somewhat improved since then, there's still some lingering issues with the game.
The gameplay itself is fairly solid. If you're familiar with other side-scrolling survival games like Terraria or StarBound, you'll be right at home. The progression system to be able to craft better items for your base and gear gives you goals to work toward. Crafting that one weapon that plows through enemies you were having trouble with is always satisfying, and having missions to clear out an enemy nest is a good change of pace from resource gathering.
The biggest issue I've had with the game is the UI. Tooltips for players new to this particular game would be helpful. There are times when the screen becomes cluttered by the menus and crafting screens, and the screens themselves will become somewhat unresponsive at times after long periods of play.
Regardless of the game's issues, which I hope can be fixed in future patches, this is still a fairly fun game, and it's good for a change from the other survival side-scrollers. Give it a look if you can.

The game is short but sweet, level design is usually consistent but not repetitive. The atmosphere is a post-apocolyptic steampunk, overrun with mind-control parasites and gigantic spiders, thriving in a world shut out from the sun by the buildings of the past.

Morphopolis, a simple yet intriguing game. A pathway made to learn the morphology of the small creatures living in unseen ground. Playing a tiny creature gathering and evolving to the next stage. It is an abstract except realistic concept of evolution.
You are first invited by the artistic style of visual artwork as you soon immerse into the world of insects. The visual layout is painted into 2-Dimensional layers which creates the 3-Dimensional atmosphere and depth. The colours are all earthy and saturated which emphasises the textural tone of the visual design. The creator really has brought out the artistic feel and paintings to life.
At first, especially during the tutorial, I had a vague understanding of story. Eventually as the levels progress you begin to understand a bit about the story. You begin as one small creature and each stage you are finding elements such as the insects prey (food) or items to assist the travel (to gain access by ‘giving/finding’ items) for the next creature. You crawl inside the head of the next creature and begin their journey. Resembling of life, there is not alot of text to guide but just the act of doing and completing the life-style of the insect.
You are set in these surreal 2-Dimensional layered artworks which is nature. Simple game of ‘eye-spy’ to progress adds to the simplicity of these game. The end level could be thought as the boss, but is basically a ‘simple’ puzzle to solve. Both getting progressively harder in each stage by either having more items to find, difficulty, and multiple items sets to find. It somewhat feels like a child-like game, but it’s creativity and puzzles, can be fun towards elderly people looking to burn some time.
The controls are fairly simply and all movement is controlled by a simple mouse clicks. The character moves by holding down the mouse as the character moves towards it. This development of movement is a really nice touch towards the essence of the lower level world. However I do have to complain that there is no quicker movement. Travelling back screens if you missed pieces is very tedious as you are trapped in the sluggish movement of your creature, but at least it does give some reason on how these bugs move. That they travel at their own pace and shouldn’t be rushed. Controlling movement around objects and towards areas can be fiddly as the direction is not always accurate when you want to turn above and right except it just goes straight up. ( -.- )... At least it has a unique style of movement and is a patient game as you find the items.
To complete it section you need to collect items, these items can be collected by the power of your mouse. By clicking on the items required they are instantly added to your ‘inventory’ of sorts. Simple mechanic but effective. It plays really well to the calm aspect of the game.
It is unlikely to replay the game after it is finished. The story will not change and levels just become easier. You can replay in the sense of finding the items again or redoing the puzzles but there is no real reason to replay the story again.
Achievements are progressive achievements (get it as you play) as they are all story-based. After each level completed you should be awarded an achievement and 100% completing this game can be done with ease.
Simple, yet fun game. Curiosity to the insect world brings interest to this game. I really enjoyed the artwork and solving the puzzles (totally did not google them, I’m smart I swear). It really engages the players down to the small level and this game should be played. I would have really liked more elements to the game such as story content.

The best multiplayer PC FPS of the past 10 years. Marred by a very rocky start (multiple bugs, some of which are still around), broken promises (to this day the game has a risible dearth of vehicles of all kinds, especially compared to its predecessor) and horrible developer PR, Red Orchestra 2 is the definitive proof that first impressions do matter. It is nonetheless one of the most authentic and thrilling infantry simulations I have ever played, while still retaining a good deal of smooth movement and playability. It feels largely like a proper FPS, unlike something like ArmA, though most of its maps can still be played in a similar fashion (with deliberate pacing and lots of caution). The engagement distances are decidedly shorter than the average milsim's (you're not going to be fighting anyone much further than 250m away), but it really does feels proper to the mostly urban Stalingrad setting. The closest equivalent in scope and execution I can think of is the Project Reality mod.
But what of the game? A class-based affair in multiple gametypes, with most Russian and German WW2 mainstays very faithfully represented. The game oozes ambition and sports a plethora of small innovations (It takes playing it so you can believe just how organic, polished and "right" the always-on free aim system feels - do yourself a favor and play the game on Realism servers), most of which directly enable the game's very tense and kinetic infantry engagements. If you have any interest and appreciation for the FPS genre at all, it will be impossible to play this game and not bear witness to its constant displays of genius and obvious evidence of superior design and workmanship. If you constantly complain about the "fact" that every FPS "wants to be COD" nowadays, put your money where your mouth is and delve deep into RO2. You won't regret it - Tripwire gave the gaming world a diamond in the rough, and has mostly polished it into a shining gem of a FPS - An accomplished example of what PC gaming is all about.

This add-on felt to be overwhelmengly obsessed with the original Half-Life and plugging HL references all over the place, instead of developing the alternate point of view. The structure is also very similar to HL: you come to work, ZOMFG! accident, aliens, then soldiers, then you're on the alien world, you come back, and mess about with teleports while obviously being had by scientists.
I think this add-on completely missed out on developing the alternate view point. It did absolute *nothing* to show you the HL events from a point of view of a security guard. You were just like Freeman, trying to GTFO from Black Mesa!
Surely an armed security guard at a secret advanced research facility has some sort of protocol for such events that happened? Even the titles that flash at the start say equipment is first priority, personell is secondary, and personal life is of low priority, yet the only thing you're meant to care in the game is your own life.
A great way to spin this add-on would've been to follow just that recipe: first you try to save some equipment but then realize it's a hopeless and stupid thing to do; we have to evacuate people! Whoever you're helping however are gunned right and left by soldiers and at the end, you're forced to abandon your job ethics, abandon your morals, and fight for your own life.
After the first 5 minutes of the game, the only thing different from this and original HL is that you can't use H.E.V. chargers. Pathetic. I'm only giving a recommendation for the sake of nostalgy.

Style over substance? Technically, yes, but only because the game's style is the best thing I've seen in ages, not because the game sucks. It's an interesting game. It's a boss rush thing, with good controls and lots of complex patterns to learn. You can choose your next battle on a top down overworld. Your goal is to beat all bosses, but there are some non boss levels where you can also collect coins which can be used to buy "upgrades". Most upgrades have a cost in addition to the collected coins so they are more like different ways of playing than better. For example, an extra heart that reduces your damage will have you fighting for longer and more likely to get hit.
So that's Cuphead in a nutshell. It's not for everyone because it is really hard. Some people like and look for high difficulty in games, others don't, so be warned. While difficulty is a matter of personal preference, I do believe I can objectively criticize the choice of making cuphead in particular so hard. Difficulty translates to repetition, meaning you will probably play each boss quite a few dozens of times before beating them. In a game where the style is definitely the selling point, this repeated exposure doesn't do the game any favors. While I was giggling and happy watching the beautifully animated bosses the first time fighting them, that sparkle died by the tenth attempt. We tend to get used to visual things with prolonged exposure. It's why visually simple games like FTL can still be so engaging and why beautiful triple A games might impress at first but can get boring quickly.  Once we get used to how it looks, what remains must be engaging enough, and cuphead will certainly not engage everyone. I'd say Cuphead has good cards on its hand but doesn't play them optimally. Or something like that. I think a campaign in the lines of rayman legends (or origins) would make better use of the style. Then again, a small team concentrated mostly on art trying to create an experience that lasts longer than a lunch break might have chosen high difficulty as a way to achieve that. Understandable but I personally don't mind short games.
I recommend Cuphead to anyone who likes hard games. And if you don't like hard games, you should at least consider getting this on a sale, if you're into that kind of animation. It's so cool looking that by the time you first rage quit the game will probably have paid itself.
