LOSE YOUR MIND. EAT YOUR CREW. DIE. REPEAT.
Sunless Sea isn't about sailing to a destination. Well it is, but it's mainly about your crew, your ship, and the stories that you encounter and make on your journey. In this game, the story is about the journey. It's about taking risks, fighting terrifying enemies, uncovering eons old secrets, and hard choices. It's sitting in stunned silence after finishing a story, gazing in terror at an enemy hundreds of times stronger than you, journeying to the surface and seeing the sun The Sun The Sun THE SUN THE SUN THE SUN THE SUN THE SUN- pardon me.
Sunless Sea has a lot of repetition. You're going to feel lost for a while. The lore is hard to understand at first, it feels like you've been dropped into the world with no background in it. But that's the fun of the game.
Being lost and alone is one of the game's major themes. You won't have any hand holding on this one. Only through trial, error, death, and repetition will you learn the game and it's lore. But that's the fun of it. I love this game because it made me feel lost. I had no idea what was going on, and it was perfect. Once I understood the gameplay, the map, the strategy, and the lore, it felt like I had lost something. It's always fun to play, but part of the magic has been lost for me. Enjoy being lost. Embrace the loneliness. LOSE YOUR MIND. EAT YOUR CREW. DIE.
Sunless Sea is honestly the best game I played this year. It's expansion, Zubmariner, is also brilliant. If you're willing to take the challenge, to learn, to be lost on a Sunless Sea, them buy them both. I can promise you, you won't regret it.

Picked this up during a sale. I own Terraria and Starbound but the latter left me burned with it's launch and follow through by the developers, but this isn't about that.
I'd been interested in Edge of Space for some time and had it on my Wishlist for a couple months before finally picking it up. A quick look through the history of the games shows I missed some of the blunder years the game held and am playing it after a UI and tier revamp so I can't comment on anything prior to the date above.
The game looks good, though I wish there were more customization items for characters, the style they've presented works well and I had no probably playing my marathon session of the game these past 2-3 days (17 hours) and the music is pretty darn good as well. Normally I listen to my own music collection during these types of games but I left the background BGM on and didn't grow to hate it.
The controls are smooth as well and how you can move is really limited to your gear and how well you can control your jet pack, using weapons can be tricky sometimes however. The game has a few different weapon types in its starter tier from the basic automatic rifle, sniper rifle, and mortar launcher. I've found myself using the sniper rifle and mortar exclusively. You have unlimited ammo but there is a reload timer but that's not why I don't use the automatic, the main reason is damage and difficulty hitting enemies. I played exclusively in a local hosted server with friends and there were times were you can't hit an enemy due to their size, movement, and shots just passing through (most likely due to the server lagging) so we found more success with the area damage of the mortar and taking the risk with the sniper rifle.
Crafting is pretty extensive as well. There are three armor types and many branches of crafting to "skill up" by using Science XP gained from mining, crafting, and hunting monsters (which is the best gainer later on) and unlike Terraria and Starbound the dungeons aren't found in the world but you rather transport to them after gaining enough coordinates to get to them. Once you enter the dungeon the rules change, you can't use your mining laser or jet pack. Having these taken away really changes how you go against an enemy as you now have to time your jumping and can't block or tunnel away from an enemy (or through a stage) and personally I feel is nice change. Unfortunately I haven't seen the dungeon boss yet as during the dungeon we had problems with the game failing to load or players games blanking to grey in the dungeon.
Overall however, I am really pleased with the purchase and look forward to future updates with the game. It does have a learning curve and some of the UI elements are weird (I've hit escape hoping to clear a open menu more times than I can count, it doesn't work) but overall at it's current stage it's fun and playable.

Outlast is a fantastic horror game, which had me on the edge with tension from pretty much start to finish. You're visiting this mental asylum (a very big one I should add) which is full of secrets and is sealed off from the outside world with no internet, and no phone signal. You're a journalist that has gone to investigate what it's all about.
You have no weapons, and are only equipped with a video camera to gather evidence and use it as nightvision. Unfortunately however your camera seems to be one past its expiry date with batteries that leak faster than the BP oil spill, so you have to be careful as to when you want to see in the dark at various points in the game.
That's all there is to it really, it's quite scary and definitely well worth playing if you want to have a challenge of getting through a horror game. Just Cause 2, while it might be old, is one of the best open-world games to date. I'm going to cover some of the specifics in this review.
For a game that came out in 2010, JC2 looks amazing. No matter how low you turn the settings, it really looks gorgeous. The sky stretches on for seemingly forever, and the render distance in this game is truly incredible. On "Low" I'm still able to see the entire map from the top of the tallest mountain in Panau. Not to mention the foliage. Trees are everywhere (except for where they aren't) and the amount of grass doesn't seem to change based on the graphics settings. The water looks great too, though the rain doesn't feel as volumetric as one would think. 9/10
JC2 is probably one of the most fun to play games ever made. The grappling hook is an awesome addition, and using it together with the parachute enables you to traverse the map quickly and easily. Gunplay, while entertaining for a while, gets repetitive and becomes just another feature.
The physics in JC2 are hilariously...werid? and that's not a bad thing. In multiplayer, grappling two cars / planes / boats together and driving them in the opposite direction produces some interesting results. Driving cars isn't anything special, but be warned about the motorcycles; it might just be me but I've experienced a small delay when turning, and while that doesn't sound bad it can quickly ruin your day.
The campaign isn't anything memorable. It provides a bit of background for Rico and the storyline, but that's about it. I didn't enjoy it that much or spend much time in it at all, because I was too busy blowing things up in freeroam.
This is a must-have for your Steam library. It's incredibly fun, and great value for the price.

I can't recommend this game if you're like me and wanted a co-op game to play.  I have like 600+ hours in Left 4 Dead because of the fun co-operative killing.
In terms of cooperative play this game has one MAJOR problem:  one of you needs to play the monster, and the monster is BORING and alone.  As the monster you run around and attack/ eat other monsters on the map until you can evolve into a bigger monster.  Once you've evovled twice(?) you have to attack a generator to end the mission, or you can just attack the medic and then kill everyone.
Fighting as the monster made me yawn, big time.  You basically just mash the mouse button and watch the health bar diminish on whatever is in roughly in front of you - your swipes and attackes don't have a physical effect on what you're attacking - if a person jumps in front of you and you swipe at it, that person contines on their lazy parabola through the air, although their health does drop.  I think the special attacks can knock them back, though.  At one point I was jumping around in a relatively small room with 4 hunters and it was just about the most boring thing I've done in a game.

The special attacks are made by choosing a number on the keyboard, which is not easy to control.  It seems the monster was designed with a "thumbs" controller in mind, which sucks for obvious reasons that all you FPS'ers know about.
You're suppose to be like a 6 story-tall massive creature but the thirt person camera makes you look like a little toy chasing around bugs in a tiny level.  Why not make it first person?  That would at least give you a sense of scale.
The level design is strange, too.  It's hard to navigate as the monster - some areas you just get stuck in geometry or dead ends and it's awkward to turn around because of the camera.  Other things don't make sense, like how I can climb some rock faces but not others.  At one point I came to a small fence but I couldn't climb it or jump over it - it was all just so awkward.
This is not the cooperative game I was looking for, mainly because there is zero cooperation with other players when playing the monster.  You may as well be playing a single-player game at that point, and I have lots of single-player games I'd rather be playing if I'm going to sit down to play a game.
They should have made two monsters against three hunters so that the monsters can get in on the co-op play, too.  It would be so cool if the monsters could buff each other or combine attacks, sneak up on their prey, etc.

I've been playing TLD for about six months now, and I figured it was time for a review.
Survival games. When I think; "Early Access Survival Game" I think, half-baked half life 2 engine survival game piece of garbage that somehow still manages to attract stupid amounts of attention, with devs that are only there to make a quick buck, and a community of troll snipers that will KOS even if you have zero gear.
The Long Dark throws all of that out the window. Half-Baked? In the literal sense, yes, but I think with just a few more tweaks you could bring it out of early access. Devs are supportive of the communty, and open to suggestions, KOS troll-snipers (a phenomenon which I like to call "Unturned Syndrome") are removed altogether by removing multiplayer altogether. No it's not the end of the world, belive it or not, not every video game is multiplayer.
The art style and graphics are lovley, and all of this alone would be enough to set it apart from the crowd of indie survival developers, coughcoughRustH1Z17DaysToDieTheFifthDaycoughcough.
But the gameplay goes further. All feels balanced, and while some argue for reduced calorie burn, some argue for increased, so I think it's best to just keep in the middle. There's no insta-craft, something I've wanted in a survival game forever, along with sleep deprivation (which this game has as well). It gives a real sense of acheivment when you finally finish the wolfskin coat you've been working on forever. I love the gunplay.
(Because hip-firing dosen't work in real life. It just dosen't unless you're supressing, and why would you supress a deer?)
There's no base building, and this might be my favorite part. I can't tell you how many times I've stumbled across someone's giant♥♥♥♥♥♥♥monument in Rust. Kinda breaks the survival aspect.
Bullet balistics work,
Animals are scary (at night more so)
The map (when you consider that it's one giant linked map) is actually pretty bloody huge
I could just go on and on.
I could talk to you all day of every thing I love about this game but I don't have the time or the patience.
I definetley recommend this game, for anyone sick of every other reskinned survival game. I know there are some who prefer to troll-snipe bambies for fun, in which case, you can head to the featured page and see about twenty games for you.
I bid you all adeiu.

*ALPHA REVIEW*
The game is loads of fun! I've played it before during The Gadget Show Live event here in UK, but we were given high-end gaming PCs with...a controller!!! Blergh, I wasn't happy about that!
Now that I got to play on my laptop - I'm very pleased with the gameplay!
The good:
> POLISHED PERFORMANCE! I was really happy to crank all the settings to the highest + TXAA and find out that the game runs absolutely smooth on my laptop...ON A SINGLE GRAPHICS CARD (forgot to turn SLI on)!
For those wondering, I'm running on an Alienware 18 laptop, sporting an overclocked i7 4700MQ (3.7GHz), 24GB DDR3 RAM and dual GTX 780M 4GB cards in SLI, but since I was playing an old game before evolve I forgot to turn SLI back on! The game didn't even need it!
> FUN! It's a load of fun ganging up on a monster like a swarm of flies on a turd :) Likewise, it's also a load of fun burning and smashing and bashing my way through a bunch of pesky hunters as a monster :)
> VISUAL CANDY! The design elements are awesome. Environments, weapons, characters, monsters -  love it!
> UNIQUE GAMEPLAY! Seriously, I don't know of a similar game...
> FREE T-SHIRT! Got one when I was testing the game at The Gadget Show Live. Thanks for that! :D
The bad:
> LOADSCREEN SIMULATOR 2014! Yes, there will be quite some waiting. Match making, character perking, loading, deployment, etc... I hope the final version will be a bit quicker in that regard, but it's definitely not a deal breaker to me.
> CONSOLE PORT! Yeah... It was bad enough to me that when I got to test this game about half a year ago we were given PCs with stupid gamepads...Now you start up the game and it says 'Press A to start'... Why do we even need that screen to begin with - this is PC!!! Sometimes controls are very unintuitive as well...
> MOUSE DELAY! Maybe I played too much Quake III (Live) back in the day and now, maybe I'm just picky like that, but even though the game runs smoothly - the mouse feels like I'm stirring thick soup. A lot of new games have this these days. Hate it. Please sort it out, lads!
> INTERNET MATCH MAKING! If you don't have 4 friends who own Evolve you'll have to rely on match-making over the internet. Since there are always new people who've never played it and also people who go AFK with all those loading screens you may end up pulling your pubic hair when your team sucks or the monster is AFK :)
Overall I'm really happy with the game so far. Just need a little less consolization here and slightly more responsive mouse aim and I'm a happy camper!

Over time with my years on Steam, and since the concept of "Early Access" was a thing. I was always a bit cautious when buying into any unfinished game, but there are quite a few Early Access games that I do quite like. This is one of those rare gems from a studio that seems to be very into the game and the community.
This game is truly a work of awesome. That being said I will say why I love it so much (down below), but that's all you need to know for the short version.
Seriously though, if you are on the fence about this game, just get it. It's good...they are making an amazing survival and box adventure (with a story mode coming soon of course.). Oh yeah, and there aren't any ZOMBIES!!! (THANK GOODNESS!!!)
:3
So I give this game my best blessing ever for an Early Access title and a survival game as well. The Long Dark is one of the only survival games where I truly felt against the elements, and nature...and just the struggle of survival. Read on though if you want the reason I give this a 11/10 and why I feel it is a truly amazing game.
First I have to say I love survival games, this finally got it right. Survival was never about the "monsters" or elements fighting against you, survival at the core is just that..."surviving". That means staying warm, finding food, looking for shelter, etc...and this game truly makes you feel like if you don't do your best to survive, find food, water, etc. you will die. Period, the game is as brutal as I would imagine nature can be.
The sounds in the game are quite good as well. The sounds range from the wind howling around outside of a cabin, or shelter of some sort, which is creepy to say the least to the winds howling around outside. All the sounds as well as ambient music fit perfectly. The sound of a wolf howling at the night, or you maybe. The sound of the wind outside is great as well and really makes you feel truly immersed into the environment and nature.
The graphics in this game while not the BEST game I have ever seen...are stylized nicely and they look good and clean. To me that's really that matters. The light, fires, and such all look really good. As do the wildlife running around either trying to eat you, or not be eaten by you...or a wolf. The night sky is pretty to look at as well, and most of the environment although similiar in some areas, is also very pretty and well designed.
The hud is almost not there (WHICH IS GREAT!), but a few times you will see things pop up on screen to let you know how you are doing. Stamina is displayed when you run, etc. This makes the game so seemless it really makes it that much more immersive.
Of course since the game isn't finished this review will get a re-write after it's done, but I will say that overall this game is well worth the full price of admission. The game is solid, survival is tough, the areas are cool, and very pretty...oh and did I mention no ZOMBIES!!! I am so very tired of those #$%@! ZOMBIES!!!
:3

A true Batman RPG that any fan would love.
I have NEVER played a Telltale game before, so I was a bit hesitant to try this, but I am so glad that I did. Every scene and every decision had me so damn engrossed.
We all have our favorite version of Batman. When we play the Arkham games, we're playing Rocksteady's version of the Dark Knight. When we watch those Nolan movies, it's his take on the caped crusader. BUT Batman - The Telltale Series lets you play truly Batman how you choose.
Telltale takes some major risks and twists with the Batman mythos which I thought paid of very well. The story reminded me such classic Batman tales as The Long Halloween or the recent Court of Owls stuff and would have have been great graphic novel on it's own, but the fact that you get to shape parts of it makes it even better.
The "combat" isn't too demanding, following what I've come to learn is Telltales signature style, but it does enough to keep things varied and hype up the tension in between decisions.
The voice cast is great too, with Troy Baker bringing his usual all to the table, to give us a very compelling portrayal of the Dark Knight. With hints of Conroy, while still really making the role his own. The rest of the cast does an excellent job as well, coming together just right to make you care and hate the characters accordingly.
There was some stutter here and there between scenes, even on my decent rig, but I've read that this was one of the minor complaints about the game across platforms.
In fact, the game has received some lukewarm reviews, but as an avid Batman fan, I thought the game was a real treat. I was hooked from the start and sat there at the edge of my seat for the finale. It took me a little over 9 hours for my first play through of all five chapters and I started again almost immediately to play with different decisions.
Grab this game right now...Because Gotham needs YOUR Batman.

I would give this game a rating of 6/10. It is not a terrible game, but not a great game either, just really mediocre.
The story starts off intriguing and promising with a reeeally satisfying first crime scene, thus making you really engaged and intrigued into digging further into it.
Later on though, at some point, the plot unfolds all at once into what feels as out of the blue nonsense and you lose interest, as it seems overly complicated and exaggerated, to the point of being funny. The fact that your own actions have very little to do with the unfolding of the plot also takes away from the excitement and the engagement with the story.

The ending... was not that spectacular either.
I found the puzzles "elementary", except for one that I found hard and a couple of others that were a little bit challenging. In general, the puzzles are very easy in my opinion, with no real "aha!" moments that will give you that satisfaction after solving them and make you self-indulge in your brilliance.
I played the game in the "normal" setting though, so I am not sure if, by changing the setting, the puzzle difficulty changes.
There is also the option to skip the puzzles, which is nice to have for those who can't come up with the solution and would otherwise be stuck and prevented from continuing the game unless they looked up a walkthrough.
The deductions on the deduction board often make no logical sense and you need to rely on luck in order to choose the right option.
The graphics are generally good and the voice acting of Sherlock Holmes is good too. I cannot say the same for the character of Watson though, as at times it feels inconsistent, switching from one emotion to the other during the dialogue - for example he may appear very frustrated at Sherlock Holmes and after Sherlock Holmes replies, he immediately switches moods and he sounds as if nothing ever happened. I found that inconsistent and to be honest, rather funny. Watson can also be quite unlikable at times.
I really liked being able to switch on my own accord between the characters at some part of the game and I also liked another variation in the control -
which spiced things up a bit.
The game generally takes you by the hand and lets you know what you should do next almost at all times, which makes it very - or rather maybe a little "too" - straightforward and linear. Also, at a couple of points you specifically need to examine some things in a predetermined order, otherwise the game will not let you interact with them.
There are no consequences whatsoever for your "wrong" choices. If you are talking with someone and you choose a dialogue option that makes them reply in a negative way, eg. not allowing you access somewhere, you can simply keep choosing the remaining options, as if the previous conversation never took place, which seems a bit weird.
The cutscenes would glitch and freeze for me - while the dialogue kept on going, the video would not flow normally.
The achievements are easy to get and you can easily have a 100% completion of the game in your library.
In general, this game is OK and has some nice moments that keep your interest going through some segments, though not consistently. It provides a means of passing the time, however, without it being an extraordinary exciting game that leaves a strong impression afterwards.
It would be best to get it on sale.

First off, I really appreciate what this studio has done in terms of graphics and music.  A+ on that.
I also appreciate the difficulty.
The mechanics are great.  Bosses usually telegraph moves well enough that you don't have to learn by trial and error.  Some mechanics give the player choice in how the battle unfolds (do you want more difficulty with more opportunities to parry?)
However, I think there could have been a few game design tweaks that would have made the game more enjoyable while maintaining a high level of difficulty.
1) hitboxes are a little stingy.  With tiny bullets and only 8 directions of fire, it can be very difficult to hit enemies while you are trying to juggle the rest of the action.
2) jump control.  The highest jump and lowest jump you can do only differ by about half of cuphead's height (probably a little more).  The ability to hop would help give the user more options instead of forcing a jump that results in a mid-air collision (basically a no-win situation sometimes).
3) parry only works at the jump apex.  Split second timing, tiny range, AND only works at the top of the jump?  Any two of these would be fine, but all three seems a bit much.

Food. Fuel. Terror. Health.
Sunless Sea is all about keeping your ship and crew afloat while exploring the weird world of the Underzee. Like any good survival horror/ rogue-like, you'll wander into situations without any idea what you're doing and run screaming from hideous monsters. Eventually though, with a little experience and some luck, you'll start unravelling the game's secrets.
But first you're going to die. Repeatedly.
Sunless Sea's strength is its wonderfully bizarre and unpredictable writing. The melding of Victorian manners and lovecraftian weirdness never ceases to be a delight, with all sorts of weird and wonderful missions sending you sailing all over the Zee. The game's systems are not quite perfect for this (a note book would have been wonderful), but a little practice and memory makes it fairly easy to work with. The game's tendency to dangle prospective missions in front of the player is keeps the interest and I found myself returning to various ports just to try and complete new ones.
Like most rogue-likes, the game can feel a little grindy at times. Earning enough cash to upgrade your ship feels a little brutal and several end-game quests appear to require nigh-impossible amounts of levelling. Learning just how to find enough cash and experience is definitely an early game challenge.
Overall, Sunless Sea is a great game, if you've got the time to play it. A tour de force of videogame writing, it'll send you on weird and delightful quests across a totally unique, if often unnervingly familiar, setting.

Seriously lacks complexity and difficulty. I wish the developers had finished this game before moving on to their next product. Banished is a nice looking city building simulation but it is completely missing all the aspects of a survival game. There is nothing that adds any real difficulty. If you do however want to have a casual and pretty looking city building simulation then Banished might be interesting for you.

This is a review in it's current state.
I understand this game is still in beta, but in it's current state I'm not a fan. I definitely see the potential of this game and can forsee it being a really fun and addictive game like Terraria. Right now it's just frustrating. Especially since this game has been out in beta for over a year and the feel hasn't changed. It's sad when 3 of my friends and I can't stand to play this more than an hour every 3-4 months we try it.
Many items that you find early in game have absolutely 0 use or in the item details it shows "Will be updated in the future" or some nonsense. The inventory feels clunky and can be buggy when swapping things in and out of your actionbars.
For those of you who played Terraria, if you enjoyed the helper dude being there to somewhat guide you in the right direction you're going to have a harder time. The beginning gives you a brief sense of direction but then it's gone. To understand what a lot of things do, you must either spend lots of time trying to figure it out on your own or look it up on the wiki.
While I feel games do need to have a little but of challenge in them, I'm not sure the start of this game goes in the right direction with that. Your mining tool is painfully slow. Your starting weapon is painfully weak. Materials needed to upgrade anything are way high. You also have lives in this game. So as you're digging down trying to find some sort of material you need to make an item you have no clue what it does, you come across some crabs that take 15 shots to kill with your weak gun and they kill you. You've spent 20 minutes digging, lost a life, and still have 0 of the material you need.
The soundtrack is nice. Which is one thing I expected after playing Terraria and Starbound. Visuals look good for the most part. The gameplay just has a long way to go until I feel it will be fun.
If you want a new Terraria style game, go pick up starbound instead. You'll be completely satisfied! Maybe in another year I can say the same about this.

Outlast is a solid horror game that takes the player through creepy environments that contain some of the most disgusting and demented things that you’ll ever see in any horror game ever. The characters that you come across in this game were done really well and they really make you believe that these are truly insane and psychotic people. The game’s story plays out in such a well done way in that you feel motivated to keep going and going all the way to the end. However, the game has two significant flaws that I want to mention. First, the chase sequences in this game can be really frustrating for new players and beginners because it can be really hard trying to figure out exactly where you’re supposed to go to survive. You might end up just running around in circles or just running all over the place over and over and over again, desperately trying to figure out where you’re supposed to go. Getting killed over and over again during a chase sequence because you still haven’t figured out where you’re supposed to go gets really frustrating and annoying. That’s the first significant flaw. The second one is the game’s ending. For me, I was really disappointed with how Outlast ends. I’m not going to say any spoilers, but the ending just made me think: “What!? Are you kidding me!?”. The game’s ending just felt disappointing and kind of insulting to the player. The ending of Outlast's Whistleblower DLC expansion was a lot better to me. That’s the second significant flaw. These two significant flaws are not deal breakers to me though. Outlast is still a well done horror game regardless and I do definitely recommend it to horror game fans

This is a meme-free review!
I love games that mess with the concepts of space and time. I’m also a retired tool-assisted speedrunner. Even without the game’s clever viral marketing campaign, I was hyped to play SUPERHOT since it came out. Finally getting to play it, it was about as good as I expected.
SUPERHOT is more of a puzzle game than a shooter. Most levels are only seconds-long in game time, but the game takes place in a perpetual state of bullet time, allowing you time to dodge bullets flying at your face and aim your shots. Aiming shots is very important in this game, even moreso than a standard FPS – you can almost never shoot directly at your opponents, you instead have to lead your shots, shooting at the empty space where they will be moments in the future. Since time is often stopped, it can be hard to tell which enemies are moving, and in which direction, so leading your shots is an unintuitive skill and it’s surprisingly easy to miss. Thankfully, the game introduces a spread-fire shotgun and a semi automatic rifle, as well as several melee options, to help you defend yourself.
It’s certainly a novel idea, but does the gimmick work? …Mostly. You’d think that if “time only moves when you do,” it means that you have unlimited time to sit and ponder your next move, but this isn’t really the case. Time still moves very slowly when you’re stopped, and it moves faster when you look around. This means that you can never really stop to check your surroundings for unexpected enemies or for bullets that are flying at you, you pretty much need to know where they are, either from hearing the gunshot or from just memorizing the level. It doesn’t help that the enemies spawn rather quietly, often behind you, and you only get a faint red glow to signal they’ve suddenly warped in. The overwhelming majority of deaths will come from getting shot by a bullet you didn’t know was coming by an enemy who spawned somewhere nearby while you weren’t looking, rather than by a miscalculated action. Another common problem is to see a stunned enemy and mistake them for dead, only to have them punch you in the back when you’re not looking. The white textureless visual style sometimes makes it difficult to judge your character’s hitbox, and sometimes you’ll try to dodge bullets only to find that there wasn’t enough room for you to dodge – again, because you can’t stop to survey your surroundings or you’ll get shot.
It mainly comes down to the design of the level. The final level in particular is super frustrating, and highlights many of the game’s weaknesses rather than its strengths. But most of the game was great fun! Hurling katanas through enemies, throwing weapons at enemies and catching new weapons flying through the air, and blocking shots by throwing props – it was all highly satisfying.
The game also has an unexpectedly meta “plot” which I found highly amusing and creepy. SUPERHOT could be considered a game fit for Halloween. I won’t spoil anything, but if you enjoyed games like Pony Island or Undertale that mess with your concept of
as the player, you’ll find a lot to enjoy here, even if the main campaign is less than 2 hours long.
Overall, a very solid 7 / 10.

Bioshock is one of the most expertly made games I have ever played. The game takes place in a ciy called Rapture, a city under the sea created by Andre Ryan to be a utopia, where people's dreams would not be limited by things such as government or morality. You play as Jack, a man in a plane crash that landed in the middle of the Atlantic Ocean, who finds a Lighthouse that leads to Rapture, now ruined and destroyed due to a war created by Atlas, a man who leads a rebellion group against Andrew Ryan, and wants to help you survive as you fight Splicers (genetic mutants created by splicing up on something called ADAM; a substance found at the bottom of the ocean that can be used for a variety of purpose. Medical, entertainment, or even getting powers called Plasmids) and Big Daddies, protecters of the Little Sisters, who hold sea slugs in their stomachs that produce loads of ADAM.
The gameplay is fantastic. Bioshock is a FPS with RPG and Survival Horror elements. You can geta total of 6 different guns throughout the game, each of which are good for certain situations. You can also upgrade these guns to make them stronger and better over the course of the game. You can also collect different types of ammo for each gun, usually there's a normal type, a type good for armored foes, and a type good for fleshy foes. Then of course, there's ADAM. ADAM is obtained after killing a Big Daddy, then by making a decision on whether or not to let their Little Sister to live. If they live, you get some ADAM, but for every 3 you rescue, you get rewards. Or, you can harvest them and get a huge amount of ADAM, but no rewards. ADAM can be spent on Plasmids and Tonics. Plasmids are you're alternative to guns, basically giving you special powers over the course of the game. Tonics give you're character direct upgrades, of which have varying degrees of usefulness. The gameplay has so many layaers of depth and strategy, and is still realy good in high-strung intense action moments. And it's just plain fun to shoot bees at a splicer, then set them on fire, and when they jump into water to get rid of the fire, you can eletrocute them and finish them off.
Even if the gameplay wasn't good, the story alone is worth the buy. I won't spoil it, nor will I reiterate what I already wrote, but know that the story of Bioshock is not only one of the best, most though-provoking stories there is, but the best part about it is that it could only work as a video game, nothing else, as the story brings up the idea of whether or not the player's choices have an impact, and whether or not the player actually had a choice throughout the whole game. It helps that all the characters in the game are very complex and believable. I could write an entire essay about how amazing the story is, but I won't because I don't feel like wasting you're time. Now, would you kindly buy this freaking game already?

Morphopolis is a beautiful slow paced hidden object puzzle game. The artwork is mesmerising, the music is calming, and although the controls can be a little awkward at times, I love how smooth the transition between panels is- including the ability to grab last second object as you're already moving offscreen.
With regards to the puzzles- the tangled string and beetle swap ones being the best in my opinion, were well thought out and had a challenging yet fun level of difficulty. In retrospect one thing I loved (Though hated at the time) was the complete lack of instruction within the puzzles. On more than one or two I would be sat there wondering what the heck I was even supposed to do (Flower placement puzzle), but it's a great way to get you thinking and working hard for your achievements.
All in all, I got this game for about 15p in the Halloween sale, and I really wish I'd paid more for it. £4 would have been a stretch, but I'd say this one is definitely worth £3. At almost 2 hours long, it's a perfect game for a nice chill evening :)

Sunless Sea is a Lovecraftian, nautical, exploration-themed rougelike.  Set in the Fallen London universe, you captain a tramp steamer across the Unterzee.  In so doing, you stave off starvation, madness, and cannibalism, and unravel stories affecting your officers, crew, and passengers.  Eldritch horrors await.
Positive aspects: The art style is fantastic, and captures the themes perfectly; the music is creepy; the writing is wry and original.  There is a hell of a lot to do, and you'll always find something new.  Even then, the company is constantly providing new content for free--in addition to a paid DLC which is more than worth it.  The all of this combines into the best atmosphere you'll find.  It oozes cyclopean terror.
Negative aspects:  If you don't like reading, you'll HATE the game.  Combat is uninspired, quite dull, and it plays a major role in the game.  And there is no character building done for you: as a player, you are dropped into a world with no explanations...figuring it all out is entirely up to you, and can take a long time.  Additionally, the game can be brutally difficult and you will die.  A lot.
The negatives can be lived with, however, because the positives are so phenomenal.  I have no qualms about recommending the game.

this game is getting a LOT of negative reviews and I see some same complaints-- No tutorial (There wasnt, there is now) - cant skip the tutorial (You obviously DIDNT read anything at all, did you?) - There's no content updates blah blah or theres not enough of X in the game yet... well I have been involved in a TON of early access projects (DayZ pops into my mind when people say "No content") and I would personally want them to re-hash and re-do gameplay mechanics before adding content, and this one has gone from having nothing but tiles, to having a power grid, to having a control system (Machines need command nodes to run) and more, and more content and bosses... went from having nothing but a few penguins with rocket launchers to terraria crossover bosses and random events... it is still early and the team may not be as large as you would like, but development is constant, and consistent-- meaning they arent working on other projects with early access money from this, at least not to the point its affecting development. Most complaints are people "I cant find ores" those people are used to easier games (Like terraria, which is fun, but face it, not hard at all) this game forces you to completely upgrade before moving much further through an exposure system (Go too low, die from the planets core radiation. makes perfect sense, but most people cry) and extremely tough enemies that dont take much damage from the starter guns.
All in all I am excited to see where they go with the rest of this project. As 2 out of 5 biomes are done as of this review, and countless systems still planned, and some tweaks to existing ones. Amazing progression system if you arent a crybaby.
TL:DR: Most reviews on this game are because people are stupid and don't read, this game is solid, and has constant updates and shows not just promise, but progress.... suppourt it if you liked terraria but it was too easy

The best WWII shooter on the market, which is able to find a sweet balance between military simulations and arcade shooters. From the frozen battlefields of the eastern Front to the tropical vistas of the Pacific, RS/RO creates an immersive environment where every step and every shot are important. With a serious emphasis on teamwork, this shooter requires people to think before they act. This is no "lone wolf" type game. You may start feeling like a child who's lost its mother, but with time and experience, you may get to be an efficient killing machine. The only downside in this game must be the painful grinding for weapons. Though they are not dramatic COD like unlocks, they are quite difficult to get. The satisfying feeling of landing a head shot with a bolt action rifle on  a moving target 90 meters away will fuel many into losing themselves for hours in this game.

I am extremely disappointed by this game. I am a huge fan of TellTale due to the stories that they tell and I love the interaction within their games. However, I bought this game now that I have time this summer to play something on Steam. Everything went smoothly until I started playing episode one. The frames began to drop like crazy, the voice overs didn't match with any character's mouths...it was a freakin' mess! I spent forty minutes trying to adjust the graphics available in-game then, I updated my graphics card -- needless to say, nothing worked. I was stuck with a lagging mouse and slow gameplay. This game is NOT PLAYABLE! I am truly getting♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥writing this review because this game has nearly been out a year and yet these issues still exist!! None of the other TellTale games have done this to me on this computer. You have two options, you can purchase this game and see if it works for you; you might be lucky but, you likely won't OR watch a Let's Play on YouTube. Trust me, it's not worth the headache trying to make this work on your PC.
As for the story that is told, I very much LOVED the story. It isn't as good as The Walking Dead Season 1, Tales From the Borderlands, and the Wolf Among Us. I would say that I would watch this game again. I liked the liberties taken and the options given. I especially loved that you can choose between being Bruce Wayne or Batman when dealing with certain situations. Now, if you're a comicbook fan of Batman and not familiar with TellTale,  you might have some criticisms but, as a comicbook fan you should be open to different versions/interpretations of characters. If you can't handle that, then go play the Arkham games.
The gameplay I've watched is the same janky, awkward TellTale engine that at times doesn't work in this game. You would think that with this property, there would be a higher budget and the quality would of been BETTER than their previous games. But, it's honestly a disappointment. I was facepalming when Bruce Wayne would literally clip through doors.  However, what surprised me was the action. I was scared it would of been weak but, it's actually quite a highlight in this game.
Overall, I was just disappointed in this game. I was so pumped and I couldn't even play the first episode! I expected better. TellTale blew it; they failed their own fans and scared off potential fans who liked Batman and wanted to give this game a try. What a shame.
TLDR: This game is broken. Story is good. Controls are horrid. Disappointment to TellTale fans and those who wanted an interactive Batman experience. Play the Arkham games for a true Batman experience. Skip this.

Let me tell you my story...
I awoke in the middle of the woods with virtually nothing. Freezing my virtually solid I wander around and eventually come to a large frozen lake with multiple Ice Fishing huts. I go hut to hut and find basic supplies before finding several cabins... all without a fire place so I cant build a fire.
I eventually come to a large ranger station... and a corpse inside... frozen. I loot his body and store what I have inside, I now have a home.
After that I walked out and started exploring and manage to find a train wreck and another corpse... this one with a rifle. I take it and continue to explore only to get pinned down by a blizzard. I barly manage to get back home to my cabin in one piece.
The next day I go out again and get some fish in the ice fishing huts hoping to get food and guts so I can take down bigger prey, Turns out though they dont give guts, however on the way back home I come across a dear carcass and 20 pounds of meat...
Jackpot
I had a treasure, enough meat to last me for weeks. I carry it all back and begin to cook it up but without a hatchet my main fire source becomes sticks which become annoying to have to deal with.
Eventually I decide to follow the train tracks by my ranger station and see where it leads me, and I come to a hydroelectric dam. Inside is a wealth of treasure and a large safe.
Figuring that is where the canadians hid their syrup I spend forever opening it, only to find a glowing premium winter survivalist super mega coat...
If the dear caracs was a jackpot this was like winning the powerball lottery, and with that coat I found something else... a pair of strong winter boots.
Tennis shoes you have been replaced!
All in all this is a great game with a lot of potential.

Let's put it this way: Bioshock is the best game ever. Ok, yeah, done.
Seriously though, this game is one of the best. This and Bioshock: Infinite have changed my gaming life. It feels and plays amazingly, on both PC and consoles, and the atmosphere combined with the story and gameplay make this an unforgettable experience.
You start out in a plane crash, and it all goes downhill, and below sea level, from there. You're thrown into Rapture, with no idea what's happening, except that you have a wrench, and by golly are you going to use it. The scenery is a dark, art-deco setting, with masks and booze everywhere, as well as dead bodies and crumbling buildings.
You are immediately introduced to the big daddy, the little sisters, but most of all, the splicers. Your main enemy, the splicers are basically nutjobs who "spliced" themselves up with Adam and plasmids. Later you learn Adam is basically a second backbone to Rapture. It is a sort of life-blood, an essence of your very essence. And little sisters harvest this. And the Big Daddies... they protect the little sisters.
Plasmids are powers in a syringe, basically. Right in the beginning, you shoot up with some electricity, and are able to zap anything in your path. You're guided by a man named "Atlas", who wants help getting his family back, and he tells you to give splicers a "one two punch!", basically zapping them then smashing them across the face with the wrench.
You get more plasmids, and more powers, and tonics to boost yourself, and weapons to arm yourself, to fight Big Daddies, mini-bosses, more splicers and different versions of them. And your only goal through all of it: Survive, and do what Atlas says.

Bioshock is a game that most people know already. Why write a review then? Because it deserves it. This game has such a great storyline with memorable characters it's hard to forget the game. The world of Rapture is a dark utopia that no one who plays is really expecting until it's too late. Once you get a taste of this game you keep comming back no matter how horrendous the world, you know you have to fight to escape.Those who love a great story, real characters, and phenomenol plot twists; this is your game. For all intents and purposes I also feel compelled to let everyone know that I saved all the little sisters. What will you be to Rapture: It's savior or it's conquerer?
On a specs level since the game is rather old there should really be no problem running it. Everything was on and high and i averaged 110 fps. It did look fantastic especially for when it came out, and honestly the magic of Rapture continues to hold strong. One note that did occur was that the setting would reset after exiting the game every now and then. Didn't take from the game, but was kinda annoying.
Pro: Amazing world that can be more or less explored. Great PC port. Varying enemy types, but a bit hectic when a lot of them show up. The power ups are crazy awesome, but I only really used the electirc power. The boss fight is a good enough battle, but a shame that the powers are kinda useless against him. Fantastic story with a great twist. Memorable characters.

This game hits a difficult spot for me, because I absolutely adore the style, the music, the graphics, the stages, all of it.
And if you can take a look at the negative reviews, it's just a bunch of people whining about the difficulty. Git gud or get out. It's not an easy game, but the ease of restarting a fight and learning boss patterns, level designs, types of enemies, etc. are all fine tuned and polished to a level I haven't seen since Overwatch.
HOWEVER,
From what I can see, both from playing and from the average time spent by players that review this game, it's not long by any sort of definition. I cleared the first world in under 2 hours, and although I can see a difficulty spike and plenty of more boss fights ahead, it doesn't seem like it's replayable. I hate likening it to Binding of Isaac, but that game had a million different ways to play it, whereas this has only several. The boss battles are great, but the problem is while THEY are very dynamic and malleable to change with each different stage — defeating one stage of a fight only to have to switch up your strategy completely is an absolute joy for a player imo — the PLAYSTYLE itself is so much of the same. I get it, it's a platformer, and to the developer's credit, they put in plenty of weapon modifications to try and switch it up, as well as not giving you a ton of money so you have to choose what you really want or need for an upcoming fight.
It's a great game, and the developers have put in inordinate amounts of effort with the bosses, scenery, style, music, everything. They 100% deserve this upvote and have earned my approval easily. I feel like the game, however, struggles in terms of playstyle and replayability. So much of what the player does is the same, and there's not a ton of variation here, even with weapon modifiers. Additionally, I don't feel like the bosses are that hard after I've memorized their patterns, and for me that kind of kills it. In Dark Souls, for example, I could always do another run through with a new weapon, build, gameplay (i.e. SL1 or no armor), and it would always be at least a little different. I don't see a ton of that here, and that's why I'm most likely going to refund it. Not because I don't like it, but because, for $20, I want to be getting more than 13 hours of gameplay, and that's the absolute max I saw on reviews.
TL;DR Music, bosses, level design, style, all fantastic. Low variability and replayabilty, and short game relative to the cost of $20.

This game can definitely keep you engaged for long periods as you invest hours in trying to figure out the game's dynamics for making town-building work. (Online guides can save you quite a lot of anguish, though you'll still need to strike a particular balance for each randomized game map's conditions.) It's much lesser in scale than SimCity/Cities:Skylines: it never goes from town to city or changes fundamentally throughout the course of a single game... but it's still a very involved process managing the ever-expanding sprawl while retaining sustainability of resources.
The main issue to note is that disasters (which are an option you can de-select at game start) are not balanced: they can arbitrarily wipe your game well into it and force you to start over. Or they can miss you entirely. Or they can reduce many hours of productivity to what amounts to starting over anyway. And they keep coming. This makes them not quite a "challenge" so much as a Russian Roulette spin on RNG. Just know that's the sort of experience the game offers... which will either make you less invested in your town, knowing it's just going to be wiped anyway, or make it more exciting for you to know that annihilation can happen any time...
But it's very fun to master. The micromanagement requires constant monitoring, but it's not overburdensome, and it's rewarding to see the little citizens complying with their livelihood assignments. Plus it's a stable game, looks nice, doesn't skimp on controls and options, and has a set of simple, melodious background tunes that sound appropriate to the theme. It's definitely been worth the purchase for me.

I'm going to write a review because I'm tired of all the sacks of♥♥♥♥♥♥saying certain games aren't worth it. The TL;DR below sums up my feelings about most of the negative reviews which are, in my opinion, generally invalid. There are absolutely things wrong with the game, and some of the reviews mention those things... but most of them are just "wah, multiplayer is buggy."
TL;DR - 1) Learn to read, 2) no one forced you to buy this game, 3) multiplayer is on a separate Steam branch for a reason.
This game is good. I haven't played it as much as I'd like, but I suspect that will change as my friends jump on the bandwagon and purchase the game. Let's take a look at good and bad with a few general topics in each, shall we?
=THE BAD= [We're bein' up-front with this.]
My complaints with the game center around lack of content. There's only so much you can do before you're out of content. You've built a fort from scratch with carpentry, you've got huge stockpiles of water in rain barrels, you're farming tons of food, and you've got all the medical supplies and weapons you could ever want. There's no NPCs to interact with so your "endgame" consists of killing more zeds. Of course, most people die. A lot. They never make it to "endgame" anyways. So from an overall point of view, it's not a huge deal. It's just kinda like... once you get there, that's it. You'll die, and then you'll do it again. That's actually part of the fun (similar in that respect to Don't Starve, albeit that game has a tech tree and pseudo-objectives aside from survival). The game is also rather boring in the audio realm, at present. I like the music but the sounds could use tweaks. Something that can be fixed with modding or with time (guessing it's on the list for the devs to work on closer to full release). Character creation is a little limp right now. You can do some visual customizations, pick a name, pick a profession (which grants a free perk of some kind), and balance some positive/negative traits such as Light Drinker, Athletic, Quick to Anger, Strong, etc. Final complaint: need moar items. More weapons, more crafting, more everything. More, more, more. Oh, and NPCs, but I already mentioned that.
= THE GOOD =
A lot of things are good about this game. One of my favorite things is that you can play it casually. On your break at work, or between classes... loot a house or two, play several in-game days. It doesn't take very long and you'll make markable progress but not be at your computer for hours. Or maybe you will, I don't know. It's also very customizable. There is a "sandbox" mode that lets you change things such as when water/electricity run out, how smart/fast zombies are, what time of year it is, how the infection spreads on an individual scale, etc. So you could do a start in the winter with extremely fast/smart zombies, or a spring start with really, really slow/dumb zombies. Up to you. Combat is also fairly intense... you'll be jumped at seemingly random times by zombies that sneak up on you, or you'll shoot a gun and quickly realize that all the zombies in a large radius are coming towards you. By the same token, that can be an advantage... moving groups around the map by shooting guns or activating house alarms. I also really like the carpentry mechanics and look forward to them being updated in the future. You can build entire bases from scratch... wall-by-wall, with doorways, stairways, windows, etc. where you want them to be. You can also make furniture (currently useless) and crates (for storing all your pens and notebooks and other crap). Farming is a requirement in longer games because electricity loss means fridges stop cooling food, and you'll be stuck with canned/preserved food and farmables. Water collection also becomes a factor: you either make trips to (or live at) one of the wells, or you set up rain barrels and hope you get enough water stored to live between storms. There's even reasons why you should have multiple safehouses. The game is also heavily moddable... all sorts of stuff... sounds, crafting, weapons, map additions, character traits, etc.
All in all, I like the game. It's not overly buggy, it receives fairly frequent updates, and the developer's mascot is a cool orange raccoon... whom I always carry in stuffed animal form on each of my characters. As far as gameplay, it's what most people would call "repetitive," but I don't think that's necessarily a bad thing. You're doing "the same but different things" each time you start a new game, and the way you make your character does have a noticeable impact on how the playthrough pans out.
My advice? Watch it on a stream, or get some unedited YouTube footage. Watch a bunch. If you like zombie/survival games and/or like what you see, get it. Maybe wait for it to go on sale if $15 is too steep for you. If you don't like it or you don't think it's worth the money, then don't buy it. I'm not forcing you. Indiestone is not forcing you. Your friend is not forcing you. Okay? Okay.

Blue Shift is another continuation of the original Half Life games. This time you assume the role of security guard Barney Calhoun, during the events of the original game. Just like the original game and Opposing Force, your main objective is to survive by assisting fellow Black Mesa Employees, using any weapon or tool to your advantage and by using your wits. Blue shift does just that.
Gameplay wise, It's still the engaging Half Life everyone knows and loves. Real Time cutscenes? Check. Aggresive and sophisticated enemies? Check. Reliable friendly NPC's? Check. Clever puzzles and well designed levels? Check. And the epic and intense gunplay that the original had? Yep, it's all here. Graphically, it's just like the previous games. The levels look as varied as ever, and the audio still breaths a great atmosphere into the game. So far, everything that is included in this expansion is good.
But it's the worst installment in the series.
And why, do you ask? Because, unlike it's predecessors, it's really short. Really, really short. And unlike Opposing Force, it didn't really add anything new. OK, maybe the HEV battery pickups have now been replaced by Body armour since you are a security guard instead of a heavily armoured scientist/soldier. But... other than that... that's it. No new guns, no new NPC types, friendly or enemy, no new level obstacles and gimmicks, no nothing. Hell, it even lacks some things from the original Half Life, such as certain weapons and an end boss. With an impressive expansion like Opposing force being released before this, I was honestly expecting to see a lot more, but instead, it feels like a watered down Half Life. It's still nice, but it could've been so much more.
Overall, Half Life: Blue Shift is a fairly decent expansion, although a tad bit underwhelming considering the content it's two predecessors delivered before it. If you enjoyed Half Life or Opposing Force, I'd say you check Blue Shift out. If you never played either of those two, this is not the best place to start. It's way too short and light on content and the other Half Life games deliver so much more. Get those instead, then buy this during a sale.

It's challenging, but it's also very playable just for its stories and atmosphere. If you, like me, prefer story over difficulty, don't let this game's genre deter you. Your experience will mostly come down to how careful you are in your exploring, and how you make your choices. In a bad situation, there's usually some way to get out of it, making the game fair even when there are many ways to die.
A far more important aspect to whether or not you will enjoy this game is its pacing. Sunless Sea is a slow game. It takes time to sail places and it takes time to unravel the stories you encounter. If you die often, you will be replaying the same stories (though this means getting a shot at a different path), and you will have to start more or less from scratch. Enjoying Sunless Sea, in my opinion, is letting yourself soak in its atmosphere, its beautiful soundtrack and its strange stories and environments.

The Long Dark is a survival game, but not just a survival game, a very BASIC survival game.
By basic I do not mean it is in any way bad. By basic I simply mean you only have to survive against one thing, the weather. No zombies, no monsters, just the weather. Just remember your Rule of Three’s: In any extreme situation you cannot survive for more than: 3 minutes without air - 3 hours without shelter - 3 days without water - 3 weeks without food, which I found to be very helpful in this game and this game sticks to this rule very well.
The game focuses on how long you, as the player in the game, can manage your supplies and maintain your body heat in the hostile environment of northern Canada in a mode called Sandbox mode, the only mode available when writing this review. Fighting off wolves for scraps of meat and hunting deer and rabbit (And Wolves if you’re brave enough) for meat. You could stick to energy bars and condensed milk, but why do that when you’ve found this shiny rifle? Eating is key to survival, believe it or not, and maintaining your calorie count to as close to 2500 is very important. Energy bars may only give you 300 calories, but a jar of peanut butter will give you close to 800. Be wise with your supplies as you don’t want them to run out, or use them at the wrong moment.
The weather effects in this game are fantastic. On a good day, you can see for miles and your body heat will barely even drop below 30 degrees, but on a bad day, you can barely see a foot in front of you and the wind is so strong that your character can only just manage to stay on their feet, not to mention how quickly your character will get cold and contract hypothermia, which will KILL YOU if you do not find shelter and warmth FAST!
The inventory system is brilliant. You can select categories such as food and BAM, there’s all the food you have. Tools? BAM! There they all are. The game works very well with the inventory and is very efficient at finding what you need. Having the right equipment is also key to surviving. For example, if you have a hatchet, you can cut up that table and put the wood on your fire. Don’t have a hatchet? Better gather those twigs and hope they last. Got a broken kerosene lamp? Repair it with your box of tools. Don’t have a box of tools? I hope you have some flairs.
Not only do you have to maintain your tools such as sharpening your hatchet and hunting knife and cleaning your rifle, but making sure you have plenty of secondary items to repair or refuel your gear. By this I mean items such as kerosene and a sewing kit to refuel your lamp and repair your clothing. You need to be rationing your kerosene as it gets VERY dark at night and choosing whether or not to repair your boots and the cost of your sewing kit, or keeping your sewing kit for later and swapping to some trainers at the risk of cold feet are tricky decisions to make, and they may make you, or end you.
The environments are stunning, like an oil painting come to life. From abandoned huts to frozen lakes, it is a very beautiful game and, I hope, like me, you stop every now and again to take it all in as it is very pleasing to look at.
My one issue I do have for this game is the difficulty. Now I enjoy a challenge, but not a grind. My issue is that, even on the medium difficulty, your character is a diabetic, hypoglycaemic wreck that will pass out without eating an energy bar every 20 seconds, drinking a pint of water every other minute, or being in the cold for an hour, whereas the easy difficulty is more realistic at the expense of no animals attacking you. I do realise this game is in early access, and I hope this gets sorted as I like the feeling knowing that I could be pounced on by a Wolf or Bear at any moment and playing on the easiest difficulty gets rid of this, but is the closest, I believe, to realistic.
This is but a small issue I have found in what looks like a promising game. When story mode gets added with the possibility of a PVE or PVP mode later down the line, I can’t wait to see how this game evolves. A good game and well worth £14. Early Acsess done right so long as it gets finished.
Edit: You probably read this thinking it should be a thumbed up game. Well it was until the developers, Hinterland, kept breaking their promises and delaying the story mode over and over again (as you can tell from the reviews going from overwhelmingly positive, to just very positive). I would change this review back into positive if they were to bring out story mode soon, but after 3 broken promises of release dates for story mode, they have moved onto a "I'll be out when it's done and we're not rushing it" approach. I fear that what could've been a fantastic game will be thrown into the abyss that is unfinished early access games. Drowning in broken promises and reluctant developers that know the longer their game is in early access, the more it’s in the spotlight. If you're thinking about buying this, don't. We need to halt purchases of this game until the developers actually achieve something and bring out the single player that they have been promising for years. Shame on you Hinterland.

While I did pick this game up for free on the Steam Sale I can say I actually paid for it via Humble Bundle a while back. This is just my summary of what the game's about. You can decide if it's your thing for yourself.
-A puzzle platformer that, interestingly, does NOT rely on a single gimmick to sell the game. It's just your character, no special powers, you can run, jump, and push things. The game frequently switches from puzzle to platformer and back and forth, some "Puzzles" just being rather difficult platforming challenges and some things that seem like platforming challenges actually being puzzles, or a mix of both.
-REQUIRES trial and error to get ahead. There are times where the game will just kill you through no fault of your own. It does often use this to clever effect, but this can feel frustrating and unfair. However as the checkpoints are very lenient I don't mind this much and just see it as a different game design approach. LIMBO treats death not as failure but a learning opportunity, though what you learn is sometimes sadly just "Don't do that next time".
-First half of the game focuses on atmosphere, second half starts focusing on some significantly harder puzzles. There is a point in the last part of the game where it pretty much just becomes purely puzzles. Thankfully IMO these lategame puzzles are actually pretty good.
-Several well-hidden secrets to find that sometimes require you to "Break" puzzles outright doing something you might initially think was an exploit. I love it when games make you think you broke them and then reveal they actually planned for you doing that.
-Platforming and general character interaction is what I'd define as, interestingly "Hyperrealistic". What I mean by that is your character moves and interacts with the environment, dies, and platforms is done in a way that feels realistic to the extreme. For some they won't like this platforming approach, and it also makes the game veeeery child-unfriendly as the kid's deaths are often pretty gruesome. It's not Mortal Kombat where the game takes joy in the fatalities, however, but in fact what happens is pretty much exactly what you would in real life, which only makes it more disturbing. This also makes the controls feel "Unresponsive" for some people but if you ask me from actually playing it just means you can't turn your character instantaneously or bunny hop like it's CS:GO.
-Very atmospheric art style. This is not a game you want to play if you want to feel bouncy and happy.
-Story is at best minimalistic and at worst nonexistent.
Overall LIMBO is NOT for everyone. That's gotta be stressed. Even if you like puzzle platformers it's not guarenteed you'll like this. However, if you've got 4 or so hours to kill you can sit down for an atmospheric jaunt that you'll probably enjoy somewhat.

"Batman - The Telltale Series" is yet another good example of Telltale's talent for storytelling. It took a different apporach to Batman's character than the Arkham series, but not for the worse. Telltale managed to show how difficult it is for Bruce Wayne to switch between his normal self and his Dark Knight persona.
The story is well-written and fits inside the Batman universe. It kept me on the edge of my seat for the whole playthrough. It also managed to pull of a few twists I did not see coming - and I'm writing this as someone who's spent hours and hours on TV Tropes.
Some other reviewers complained that the game felt like "just one very long cutscene". I have to say: Yes, you do not do much, action-wise - except for the many quicktime events the game is littered with and some deductive reasoning that Batman has to do as the "world's greatest detective". But everyone who knows Telltale's other works will not be surprised nor disappointed by their game design.
In conclusion: Great story, fun to play and totally worthy of the name "Batman".

--- Alpha Review ---
Seeing as this is the alpha-version of the game you, the reader, should take into account that there's alot more content waiting for the full release.
Taking that into account myself, i have VERY high expectations for the full game myself.
At the point of writing, i spent at least three and a half hours playing at least around five (very intensive) matches.
During these matches i played with three of my friends versus the same random guy who shouldered the role as the monster.
I can describe all of these matches with one word: Awesome.
My friends and i discussed more than once how we should flank and pin down the monster, we screamed in anger as one of us got killed and we cried tears of joy when we finally brought down the huge beast!
Evolve holds a very promising future, when you play with a competent team that actually communicates the game brings alot of intense, heart-pounding and glorious moments.
Not only is the game concept itself interesting, the execution of it all is top-notch, the maps are full of dangerous wildlife and hidden paths for the monster.
As a hunter you will find yourself spending many hours on chasing the monster while planning hasty ambushes with your friends, truly a exciting experience, especially once you get to learn all the characters, maps, wildlife etc.
For a alpha, with all its glorious bugs, i am very satisfied as a gamer and i am perfectly sure that Turtle Rock Studios will deliver!

Disclaimer - This review was based on the Alpha Weekend and Closed Beta builds of the game. I have not had a chance to play the new game modes or the new characters included in the final version. My "Not Recommended" rating was meant to dissuade people from pre-purchasing what I consider to be a 'wait-and-see' quality game, and as such the review is less applicable now. If I ever purchase the game, I will update with my final thoughts. I will leave it up for now becaue 1) the comments are hella amusing and 2) I think some of my criticism still applies to the final product, if the professional reviews coming out are any indication. Thanks for reading!
ORIGINAL REVIEW(S) -
A QUICK CLOSED BETA UPDATE:
(Also, note that my hours in closed beta aren't reflected in the 4.8 above)
Played some more in the closed beta. I realized that a lot of the people saying "you're playing the game wrong" in the comments are nicely outlining one of my issues with the game. There's a specific, pre-defined way you're 'supposed' to play, and the challenge is in sticking to that script. In multiplayer games, the human element allows incredible breadth of strategy and personal style - but Evolve is constantly trying to get you to play it on its terms. By so rigidly structuring each match, Evolve is severely limiting its own replayability. This is reflected in the current pricing situation: it seems to me like they are trying to set themselves up to make most of their profits in pre-orders by bundling content in different ways, because interest in this title isn't going to last very long.
I hate being so negative, because I really wanted this game to succeed. I hope Turtle Rock rediscovers the spark that brought us Left 4 Dead with their next title.
ALPHA WEEKEND REVIEW:
This game ticks all of my boxes: it's a unique, asymmetrical, jetpack-fueled FPS that relies heavily on teamwork (or being a sneaky ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, in the case of the monster). Sounds great, right? Game of the year material, yeah?
Not
.
It's in alpha, so you have to take the following complaints with a grain of salt. I do feel, however, that my issues with the game are deeply rooted in the current design and won't be fixed with more content or polish. I would be very surprised if any major changes are made this far along in development, and I think it would take some major changes to fix the issues with Evolve.
First off: GRAPHICS. It's very pretty. It's running off of Crytek, so this is to be expected. Great textures, models, and monster animations. But the visual design is terrible. Everything is a muddy grey color, and they've got the 'dark and moody' dial cranked up to 11. It gives all the levels a very samey feeling. And it doesn't help that the  -
LEVEL DESIGN is homogenous. The maps are all fairly small, mostly open, with a fantastic amount of verticality. There are places to hide as the monster, and good chokepoints for the hunters. The levels are decent, but at this point too similar (hopefully the new maps will spice things up a little). The issue is the size of the monster prevents the level design from influencing the mechanics of the game in any meaningful way. Whenever you encounter the monster (outside of the final defense), the battle will play out similarly no matter where you threw down the 'mobile arena,' with little influence from your environment. And it doesn't help that the -
HUNTERS have few meaningful decisions in combat and otherwise. Your class defines pretty strictly what you will be doing in combat. Use lightning gun until its cooldown kicks in, switch to assault rifle until cooldown is up, switch back, place mines, repeat. The classes DO interact in interesting ways, with the support providing temporary invincibility to one player, the medic healing, and the REALLY interesting ability to tag spots on the monster with a sniper rifle to create vulnerabilities. The problem is that these abilities are so specialized, and you have such a small repertoire, that sometimes it feels like the battles are playing themselves. It only takes a few encounters with the monster before things start to feel repetitive. This wouldn't be an issue if the gunplay itself was interesting, but aside from the jetpacks, it's some of the most uninspired, unsatisfying, console-esque 'hold button while reticle is in vicinity of enemy'. It probably feels great for console owners, but for PC shooter fans, this is some mediocre combat.
The hunting itself is lackluster. For the most part, you bumble around, sort of following the monster's path, sort of just hoping you'll run into him. I suppose this could be better with a more skilled group, or a group of friends who communicate well - but relying on friends for fun is really lazy design. The idea of 'hunting' is so central to this title that it really needs to FEEL like you're tracking down a monster, which it rarely does. It mostly just feels like you're chasing something much faster than you. That's not a super gratifying experience. There are environmental hazards that insta-kill you if you teammates don't rescue you quickly enough, which is frustrating. I guess they're there to spice up the combat, but I've never seen them act as more than a nuisance. Luckily, it's much better as the -
MONSTER: the best times I've had playing Evolve were as the monster. Knowing when to engage, the constant feel of being hunted, the tense moments of vulnerability as you evolve into the next stage, the terror as you're surrounded by a dome of light and can no longer run away... It's good stuff. I can see myself putting a lot of hours into this game in the hopes that I can play as the monster.
CONCLUSION: This feels like the developers plucked an interesting boss fight from a larger game, and then tried to duct tape a bunch of stuff on in order to justify selling it as a standalone experience. If there are major changes made in the next few months, they might make that duct-taped mess interesting enough for this game to have staying power. But I'm not holding my breath.
EDIT: I've thought a bit more about Evolve, and I've come to the conclusion that another reason (and perhaps the main reason) it fell flat for me is the pacing. Every form of entertainment has an ebb and flow of action that keeps the audience engaged, and I feel Evolve was sorely lacking in this department. Even when you're hot on the heels of the monster, hunting has little tension as the hunters, but as soon as the mobile arena comes down tension is immediately ratcheted sky-high. There's no natural ebb and flow, there's just periods of mild disinterest with the occasional intense battle. I sort of feel like the 'mobile arena' is too contrived of a concept, and that there should be objectives during the match to force confrontation. This would allow the designers to control the interest curve and keep people engaged at the same level for the length of the match.

Jim Sterling is right about this game.  The more you know about it before you play, the less you'll get from it.  Yes, it is short, you'll finish in an hour and a half.  It has no achievements or trading cards.  The challenge in this game is not strategic or dextrous, but intellectual, and the more you invest yourself in proceedings the more you will get out of it.  It has the potential to change a person for the better more than any game I've ever played, and it's an experience you'll never forget.
Frankly, I would never otherwise recommend a game as short as this for this price, but this one is worth it.  Think of it like a movie, but with a story that can only be told through an interactive medium.  I hate the term 'walking simulator' because it is derogatory and dismissive, but if that is what the genre is to be called, this is the best walking simulator of them all.
