The premise of the game is pretty fun. If you'd like to have an early colonial America simulator, I feel like this is pretty close to it. A group of people leave their home country to venture into the wilderness and survive.
You can choose from millions of generated maps, a handful of climate conditions and starting scenarios. Each one brings a slightly different flare to the game. In addition, their are random disasters, though these can be turned "off" - except for disease outbreaks. Resources like wood, stone, and iron must be ballenced, and you must make tools and clothes to keep your citizens productive. Additional resources like booze and a church keep people happy, while Herbalists and Doctors keep people healthy. Schools make people more efficient, and a variety of food sources ensures that if something goes wrong people will survive!
The base-game is very entertaining to play itself, though saves take a while to load no matter what you run. The game handles mods beautifully, and the mod-manager lets you know what mods are going to conflict.
The best mods by far are Colonial Charter, which adds more of that British America 1700's flare. I'm blanking on the others, but someone made a mega-pack that contains of the best mods (about 50) for the game. So you could play forever and still not have gone through everything! However, mods take a long time to load, so if your on an old computer I would best beware (even my gen 6 i7 and brand new SSD have a bit of trouble with all the mods and assets they add).
10/10 would recommend buying.

As an experienced player of Telltale games I jumped into this title not expecting too much. Telltale have made very similar games for a few years now and they keep the concept going mostly steady. After a few letdowns with some previous titles I didn't really set my bar high for this game. However, im glad to say I was very impressed by this game and the improvement Telltale has made to this title.
This game features a good set of hard choices to make, however it's hard to say how much inpact it will have for the future, but they are really tricky and you have to stop and think for many of them. The choices (without spoiling) were most of the time pretty equal in procent between players choosing A or B, meaning that more people then me found that there was a lot of hard picks to make.
I learned a lot about the villains from another perspective in this game, like catwoman, two-face and joker before they got their role. You get the chance to try and change who they become and which you wanna help or try and become friend with. It's a very interesting perspective, especially since the other batman games only follows a set line where the villains are bad guys, while this game let you make more decisions and learn to know them better. This give you as the player more feelings for them and it's an effective way of doing story-telling.
This is a game focused on Bruce Wayne, his family legacy and a lot of things I didn't know came up. I have played all the other batman games and watched the movies, however I haven't read the comics so I still have missed a lot. Therefore it's hard for me to compare the two and whats completely new and what is taken from the comics. But this game added a lot more for me even as someone who have played previous games, as it doesn't focus as much on the joker and more about the events before the other games.
A new villain is also included in this game, which is refreshing since Joker made many appearances in the other batman games. I won't spoil who this new villain is, but let me just say its very interesting and the story takes many turns in directions I didn't see coming.
Telltale is extremely good at making you like characters to later be screwed over by them or killed. This is something they have done in previous games as well and you can roleplay as more of a good guy, evil and mean, or try and be neutral. I haven't seen Telltale make the decisions, choices and characters feel this impactful since The Walking Dead, which is a very good thing, for those of you who haven't played that title. It's very exciting and more interesting to play the Telltale's Tales From The Borderlands for example, in my opinion.
The QTE's have been improved I would say. I feel like there's less fighting in this game then the others and more focus on dialogue, but there's still a decent amount of it, so stay away if you hate QTE (quick time events - basically pushing buttons in a said order). They made it better and somehow makes it feel impactful in the fights, but of course the story is the strong point of this title.
Batman is known for solving crimes and searching for clues on crime scenes. Well like the other batman games you have some of that in this game as well. It's pretty simple but fun anyway and it's a welcome change in gameplay from just QTE's.
You can play the game with keyboard + mouse or with a controller. I played most of the game with an xbox controller since it's mostly a game you can kick back and watch, like an interactive movie where you press buttons once in a while. But whatever you choose to play with works. The game runs at 60 fps locked and I think they have improved upon the PC-port, options menu and graphics since previous games. The style is the same but some better textures for example. They also give you some more choice this time around, for example you can pick the colour of your gear which will be unique for your playthrough.
The episodes are between 1-2 hours each, the first one is always a bit longer. Five episodes in total so you are looking at about 6-10 hours, depends on how fast you figure out the clues and how much you look around. I can't say I have any complaints about this game, I'm actually very impressed! I would put this among my top Telltale games actually and give it a big recommendation to fans of point 'n' click, Telltale games in general or fans of Batman and superheroes. Love it!

Allright, time for a re-review.
Blue Shift is the last of the side stories for the original Half-Life and once again it was made by Gearbox with help from Valve. But unlike Opposing Force, Valve decided on the story so we won't get any BS Race-X aliens. Anyway, this Side Story lets you play as Barney Calhoun. (The REAL one.)
However, Unlike Gordon and Commander Shepard, G-Man doesn't do a damn thing and You're on your own for this one. So yes, this is the ONLY time in the Half Life series (As of this review) where you work for a happy ending and you GET a happy ending. (Until HL2, that is.)
The weapons that you can use are way and i mean WAY fewer than HL or HL:OF BUT, with the console you can access HL's Weapon list.
If you wanted to know Blue Shift's Weapons: (Crowbar, 9MM, Revolver, Shotgun, Rawket Lawnchair, Satchel Charge, Hand Grenade and the Snarks.)
Not as much as Opposing Force, but let's be honest: We are only going to use the shotgun, aren't we?
In all, if you wanted to have a quick stroll and look back through time to Black Mesa without the Slog-Fest of Opposing Force or don't want to go through the un-holy mess that is HL's Xen, I would go for this game.
For PC and Sega Dreamcast, It's Half Life: Blue Shift released in June 12, 2001!
PS: this game does NOT have the "ACTION PACKED AMURRIKIA SAVES THE DAY BY KILLIN ALURRENS" or the "WHAT HAS SCIENCE DONE?!?!?!?!?" style that the other two games have. You have been warned.

Klang is almost good. There is a good game under it, somewhere, but the amount of very significant problems will keep most people away, myself included.
The amount of visual noise is mind boggling. 85% of the time, I didn't know how I died or what hit me. For example, you know you have to press a button by a cone in that direction. You know what's also a cone? An attack. They also have more or less the same colors, so good luck parsing what's on the screen.
The game also has an excessive amount of explosion effects that obsfuscates the most important kind of information...
In a reflex based game, the
you need is to make every gameplay element distinct. This is one of the worst games I've played in that regard.
Then, there's the controls. Using the analog stick for discrete input (8 directions) is not a good way of doing things. But that's what this game does. The keyboard controls aren't much better, since you have to press two keys at once to get the 8 directions. Playing with a keyboard, with a ton of buttons, you have to press two keys at once...
Again, this is a game where reflexes matter, and pressing two keys at once is awkward and sometimes registers incorrectly because you accidentally press one key before the other.
Then, there's the fact that levels are extremely short and not at all song oriented. In fact, the more "song oriented" levels are about 1 minute long at most.  This leads to two problems.
The first problem is that this simply doesn't work as a traditional rhythm game (in any way) where can just pick different tracks to play through and enjoy your time. 1 minute long isn't enough to get in the flow or have any real progression. You get 3 or 4 short sequences and you're done...
The other problem is also related to the unorthodox control scheme and the amount of clutter:
Maybe you can learn how to parse all the information and press the right keys intuitively. But that requires some amount of practice. Of which this game has none. Because everything comes in such short sequences, you never get the change to really learn anything. It has a huge amount of checkpoints, so you rarely play for more than 30 seconds at a time. And the game doesn't reuse many elements. One level is rhythmic combat, the other is stealth, the next is platforming, etc. Too fragmented and never gives the player a chance to learn the game.
It's rare that I want game to have filler, but this one definitely needs it. Again, most of my time with it was spent in frustrating, not knowing what the ♥♥♥♥ was going on from all the visual noise and getting tripped up over what keys to press.
Finally, there's the fact that there's barely anything "innovative" in here. It doesn't push the genre beyond anything. The platforming and the rhythm part are completely independent of one another. Basically, you have to press the right arrow keys on time while also running left and right to dodge beams. That's it.
It's just multitasking. The game doesn't use the platforming in a rhythmic sense at all, except wall jumps...
Before the Echo was a really good example of a rhythm game that actually tried to do things differently. The game was difficult to play, at first, and involved a good deal of multitasking. But it also had a much better structure, allowing you to get used to the gameplay before presenting the real challenges.
140 is a rhythm platformer that is really good as well!
This game isn't, really.
And it's unfortunate, because the game has a very unique artstyle. It looks very unique and the developer is clearly talented to make all this!
And when the game worked, it was good! Unfortunately, it barely every worked for 20 seconds straight.
I tried to give it a good chance. I finished the main ending, then completed all of the bonus stages for the extra ending. I also tried "hard" mode, which is really just a sped-up version of the main mode (which, come on, now the levels are 45 seconds long instead of 1 minute! And the music doesn't sound nearly as good what are you doing?).
I see some reviewers having 10+ hours, one even 90. This game is extremely short, could be easily finished in 1 or 2 hours if you can parse things. So I assume they got over the clutter in time and actually started enjoying their time.
I tried, and got a bit better by the end. But then, with all the levels being so short and extremely narrow, I didn't think it was worth to keep playing. It's not like you're mastering a song. Instead, you're mastering very short sequences that while rhythmic, don't have much to do with the song.
So yeah. Not to my liking at all. But I think there is a fun game here. Here's hoping KlangM (his next game) will improve where this one fails so that I can try the good game this is supposed to be.

I sat here for several minutes trying to come up with something to say about this game.
But when it really comes down to it, it's one of those experiences where you can't explain why it's so good without ruining it. Much like The Stanley Parable, I suppose, but besides that one key similarity, the unexplainable experience, it's really entirely different.
The Stanley Parable made me rethink the concept of narrative.
The Beginner's Guide made me rethink the concept of empathy.
More, spoilery details about my experience:

This game is marketed like as a clone of Tererria. This is only partially true. I really like Tererria, but I don't like this game. I understand that this game is still in early development, but based on what I have seen so far it is headed down the wrong path.
1. Everything is much bigger in this game. The character is bigger, the blocks are bigger, everything. This means you cannot fit as much of the game on the screen at a time, so you cannot see as far.
2. There is no map. I use the map all the time in Tererria to find my way around and locate resources. One of the things I like about the map in Tererria is it shows open areas near you, so you can dig towards them. Since this game does not have a map it also does not have this ability. Finding resources is extremely difficult. I have spent hours digging around and ohly found very limited usable resources. Instead Edge of Space has a radar system that you have to craft, and beacons, which you also have to craft. Since it is so hard to find resources it is very difficult to find enough to make these items and so it is difficult to find your way around. Even with the radar, all you get is a little blip on a small radar screen to try and find your way around. This is so much less effective than having a map.
3. So far I have not found any hidden treasures. In Tererria treasure chests and breakable containers are a great way to get resources and gear early in the game. This game does not have these so you have to manufacturer everything yourself. This results in the game moving a lot more slowly.
4. This game does not have biomes like Tererria. For example every Tererria map has desert, jungle, forest and ocean biomes. These go along way to add variety and keep the game interesting. Since this game does not have these it gets boring really quickly. In tererria you also have weather and other events, like blood moons and such. This game does not have anything like that.
5. Weapons suck. The only weapon you have is a gun and it has very limited ammo and has to take time to charge. This is a big pain because if you get attacked by a mob you quickly run out of ammo and have to run away until it charges back up. This makes figinting really difficult and not fun. In addition gun are not good close range, so if the enemies get close you will not be able to hit them. Upgrading the gun is also a slow process. You first have to get enough experience to unlock the plans for a new weapon before you can build it. Since gathering experience is slow it can take a really long time before you are able to upgrade.
6. This brings me to my next dislike. The experience system is completly messed up. There are 18 different categories for experience, and upgrading them depends on which items you pick up. This means you may find a lot of upgrades for furnature, but not for weapons, which has happened to me, and so you have great items to place in your base, but really crappy items to fight with. I like Tererria much better because you only have to gather the materials and you can make anything.
7. You cannot use items directly from your inventory. To use an item, even things like health and other consumable items you first have to put them in your quick bar and then switch to the item and use it. Then when you have consumed all of them it stays in your quick bar with a big red X over it. I would prefer that the item was removed from the quick bar when it was used up. Your quick bar has a very limited amout of space, only 8 slots, so you will be juggling things in a out all the time.
8. Detail screens are split up into 4 different screens. In Tererria if you hit the esc key you see your inventory, weapon, item, and vanity slots and everything else. In Edge of Space you have to hit I for inventory, V for crafting, C for armor and item slots, and L for Experience. The 4 different screen also cover each other up and cannot be moved. So if you try and drap something from the inventory to the armor slot you have to juggle the two screen and make sure they are not covering each other or else it is impossible.
9. The bug reporting system is lousy. When you go to submit a bug you fill out what looks like a standard email form with a place for your email, a subject, and a message. However it is extremely limited in that if you make a spelling mistake or want to go back and clarify something you cannot just use your arrows or mouse and go back to previous text. The only way to go back is to use the backspace key. This means you loose all your typed text up to where you want to change.
All I can say is I am glad I bought this game on sale because if I had paid more than $5 for it I would be extremely upset. Right now I am willing to wait and see if it gets better.

Cuphead is a great game, simply put. That being said, I think it does have its drawbacks and problems.
For one, the game is relatively short. Depending on how much time you have on your hands and how "good" you are at games like this, it shouldn't take more than a week to beat it. This is remedied by the fact that its difficulty and replayability pads out the game's length. Plus, its cost of $19.99 USD is pretty fair.

Secondly, despite its positive effect on padding out game length, I have had issues with the game's difficulty. Most times it was completely fair, but there have been times where you question how you were supposed to dodge a projectile or attack. It is a difficult game and you WILL have a hard time beating it. So, keep that in mind as you play it.
Besides that, the game is a beautiful experience with art, music and aesthetics that are pleasing on so many levels. The customization option is also great in giving players a choice that suits their play styles. Ultimately, I'd recommend this game to anyone who likes a challenge and enjoys the appeal of the 1930's style of cartoons.

The big dealbreaker for this game is that half the time the rhythm game element just flat out does not work. Like, "doesn't sync up properly to the music rendering the game nearly unplayable" doesn't work. There are times it does but those moments are almost exclusively when you are not doing any platforming, and surprisingly I found this happening even during the boss battles where you'd expect the most polish.
At the start of the game I was going for all S ranks. I gave up on that by the second boss at which point the game had become completely unreasonable and a lot of the faults with the rhythm game element had started to show. But that's also the point where the level design became genuinely kind of bad, the boss has you attacking to spawn platforms and making basically any failure an instadeath. That's one thing. The health system in this game is rendered nearly useless when 90% of the time you're just going to be instakilled by a laser or fall into a pit and die. Why even bother, life regenerates really quickly normally anyways. But yeah the game did not really improve from there.
It's also fairly short - completing the normal ending took under three hours for me, including a lot of replaying earlier levels for S-ranks, and going out of my way to find the bonus levels and play those too. And the extra ending didn't take even an hour on top of that. For a $15 game I don't feel I would've gotten my money's worth but fortunately I got this fairly cheap. Still.
The game never really develops its platforming much and most of the game is focused on the combat, which is incidentally the broken part of the game. So yeah. Woops. There's some real frustration in the later levels where the attacks and the music are just slightly out of sync so that something that should become mindless as soon as you see the notes instead becomes another thing you have to keep track of.
And there's so much visual clutter in this game that it's way harder to keep track of things than it should be. The constant neon effects are one thing but the way everything changes color when you build up a combo or are at low health just makes it all that much more difficult to keep track of stuff, especially when you're trying to platform, attack, and dodge instakill lasers all at the same time. This gets especilaly bad in the later boss fights and most of the extra world but it can stll be a problem before that. The visual style looks decent at first sure but it's very unchanging and eventually rather monotonous to look at.
The soundtrack is also, to my ears, hot garbage, but I am admittedly not a big electronic music fan. It just feels... really samey & rather basic. A lot of the same synth tones, usually a basic beat and bassline with a different melody overlaid on top of it. There are some moments, usually during the climactic moments of a boss battle, where I can kind of get into it but for the most part I find it pretty generic and forgettable and often borderline obnoxious.
So uh yeah. What do I like about this game then? Well, the concept itself is actually really good, but the execution itself is just not there in so many ways. And it's a shame too, this did look pretty neat but I didn't enjoy my time with it past a certain point and definitely won't be bothered to complete all the remaining achievements, especially considering how difficult some of the later ones are. Entire game without dying? Yeah no. Speedrunning? No sir. Getting every level perfect at 1.5 speed? Jesus christ, no. I don't think these achievements are necessarily bad to have on their own but with how little the game functions at its core it's insanity to be expecting this level of perfection from the player, when the game does not give it in return.

The game of Evolve pulls you into the future where mankind employs high tech hunters to purge planets of alien life forms that may be a threat to them. Paving the way for human expansion or at least that was what seemed to be conveyed to me while playing this game. On the main page for evolve there is no real story involved. Merely fluff like "man vs nature".
Obviously they felt there shouldn't be much of a story. No compelling back stories on the hunters or even how the Kraken misses its long lost love which made it lash out at the humans moving in on his backyard or how the Goliath longs for a little human named George or was it a rabbit?
This game was a lot of fun initially. Whether I was the monster or a hunter. The monster player will run away from the hunters, upon reaching stage 2 the monster would engage the hunters. Testing their resolve to the chase. Fleeing when the monster has taken more damage than it is comfortable with.
In the role of the hunter, you will need to pursue and damage the monster before it has a chance to evolve. The best stage to kill the monster is evolutionary stage one. At stage two, the monster will be a hand full and at stage 3 the hunters will be in for one hell of a fight.
I was so looking forward to this game. Yes, one could say that I was hyped. Until I played it for a few hours. Then I started to realize that it was fun but there needed to be more to this game. The only event that really forces the hunters and monster into a fight is the power relay. A few times when I was playing the monster, I evaded the hunters the entire match. The hunters were hot on my heels and as soon as I was able to attack the power relay by evolving. I made a B line for my objective, out running the hunters and destroyed the power relay before they are able to interrupt my animation of destroying it.
As a hunter, I played a couple of matches where the monster player evaded the entire time. This turned the match into a 15 minute jet pack simulator. Even with being able to double tap the jump button (This would launch you forward eating up extra fuel but allowing you to cover more ground.) I was always barely out of range to dome the monster. Some monster players are just more mobile than others, they pay attention to where the hunters are and try not to be in one location for too long. Chasing a monster for 20 minutes can become boring and if hunters are tired of the chase from the start. They can just wait at the power relay while the monster reaches its full potential.
I have a feeling that this will be the game at release, I have play tested a lot of titles in alpha and beta. Game play doesn't typically change a lot.

I enjoy playing this game. Hunter or Monster... it is fun. The majority of the time I win the match. But because of how simple the game setting is I can't throw money at it. Hunters chase monster or defend point from the monster. There are 5 players involved. One player plays the monster and four players are hunters. Each character have different abilities for the most part. The monster runs around eating animals it has killed or that are dead to gain experience to evolve (aka level up). Maximum monster level is 3.  The hunters do not level. What you see is what you get.
There is currently only 2 maps from what I could tell. With random weather effects. Once the monster is level 3 it is able to attack a power relay. Why? Who knows.... he just wants to destroy something. Plus this forces the fight to one area. There is a timer that will expire in favor of the hunters if the monster does not kill the hunters (If any one Hunter character including Daisy dog lives for a certain amount of time the dead Hunters will respawn.) or if the monster fails to destroy the power relay. This is so that the monster doesn't simply run around the map for an hour evading the hunters.
The overall plan for this title seems to be the same as what we are currently exposed to in game. DLC is planned to add additional monsters. Hopefully additional characters and maps will be provided with said DLC along with new game modes. Only having an arena style mode on a jungle like map or any other map will get old pretty fast. Especially since there is only 1 person as a monster. Don't get me wrong, I like the concept. But I already found myself asking "Will my play time on this title rival Left 4 Dead?"
In L4D I had 339 hours played and in L4D2 I clocked in 466 hours. One could say I played the diddly out of those titles. So will this title hold the same interest that those had? Why the benchmark? Because this is the same studio that created L4D. I found that my question was answered the first night of the alpha when I stopped playing. The only reason I had stopped was merely because the novelty of the concept was wearing off.
I played it the next day with friends. But even they were questioning the longevity of Evolve. We came up with a number. Odds are (if it remained as it is currently) we would only play it for a couple of weeks and then move on to the next game. I am sure others would not agree with my conclusion. But this is what would happen if I purchased this at release.  In the current day of gaming, I need a game more compelling and challenging to keep me engaged for a long period.
L4D was pretty simple you say? But there were more dynamics involved. When playing as a survivor everything wanted to eat your face and you had 4 players playing unique infected.  There were trigger events that would increase the danger.  In Evolve, the Hunters just run past 99% of the environment without a real issue. Minus the trapping creatures that pop up once in a while. On the monster side of things he simply kills what he can and eats for xp. It's too simple, I need more from this game in its current state.
PS: Please don't even get me started on the progression system, Daisy still needs to lick up 4 people from dying in order for my Trapper to unlock further areas of her skills.

could've been a lot more... as it is, it is little more than a glorified interactive art gallery. don't get me wrong, the art is pretty darn awesome (except that last bug in chapter 5 looks really bad for some reason). the landscape makes me wonder if insects see the world in such a vivid way with their different eyes and biology... unfortunately, there's really little else other than the art and immersive ambient music.
the controls are annoying. the bugs move terribly slow. the hidden objects are fairly easy to find, but making the bug move to and fro to access different screens... ugh. the puzzles are interesting, but without ANY bit of instruction, they are basically mocking your ability to guess what exactly you're supposed to solve until you "get" it. the "flower draughts" especially... how are you supposed to guess that you have to move those flowers in that particular way? frustrating and needlessly so. puzzles should at least have a hint on your first move, so it's subtle but not completely dense.
my final comment is on the "plot". the insect you control "morphs" as you progress through the 5 stages; however, your bug actually only metamorphoses once (from 1 to 2). for the other progressions your bug actually changes SPECIES, which not only does not make sense, it also feels awkward. while you are picking up pieces of a fallen bug, you may be thinking: i'm helping this fallen bug in some way. but it turns out... nope. you end up burrowing into its carcass and somehow magically end up "driving" the bug you were fixing. what kind of weird is that? it could've been a charming little "bug helps bug" story, or an informative "bug eats bug" science lesson; instead it is neither... and it doesn't make sense as a sci-fi or fantasy either -- why morph into another bug?
the ending doesn't feel satisfying either. i was fully expecting a good cutscene to explain what my bug was trying to do... but nope. nothing. just back to title screen. i felt really cheated at the lack of any resolution... which is why the whole "game" really came across as little more than an animated gallery.
get it when it's on sale just to see the fantastic hand-drawn art style with the mostly-spot on miniature life animation. otherwise, you can get much more satisfying puzzle games on steam for less.

A neat concept plagued by a prodigiously terrible execution, Evolve is an exercise in futility. A verbose review would only serve to do it justice in some light so I offer you the following:

As of the Big Alpha;

-No variety, next to no replay value. If you have been fortunate to play 5 rounds as the 5 roles, you have seen all this game has to offer (at this time). It's unclear whether there would really be any greater contribution by the time it's in full release.

This game is an interesting one. Despite the plethora of first person survival games on Steam, and everywhere else to be honest, this game changes the formula. While most games might have a focus on crafting and an overall threat of zombies and alike, this game takes the divergent path. The crafting system is somewhat muted and can be played entirely without, and the only real threat is the elements. While there are prowling bears and stalking wolves among the vast frozen wastelands, they are easily scared off with a flare or a torch, or even a gun. The real enemy is nature itself, as the player is made to survive the cold, harsh winds, freak blizzards and minimal shelter. The gameplay essentially breaks down to traversing the areas looking for shelter, food, water, and other essentials in order to keep death away for another day. The tricky part about this is that in each area the food and water are minmal enough to make it so players feel the need to move on in order to survive.
While one can subsist on melted snow and the animals of the area, eventually either boredom or lack of rescources will cause the player to move on. This is where I find the one real problem I have with the game. Because of the need for exploration, I found myself often moving through areas quickly in order to find more useful materials. This is good for the first few hours because I was always seeing something new. Then I died, and respawned. The problem now was I had to traverse the same landscape I had. This wasn't a major problem because the game is well varied in each area. There was certainly never a moment where I could become complacent, because the game doesn't let you. The moment you think you have the game down, it decides to rain the all singing all dancing♥♥♥♥♥♥show of this games brutality upon you.
Allow me to demonstrate: I was backed into a corner with a flare in front of me and a rifle in my hand, two bullets to my name. There were, conveniently, two wolves ahead of me. The ultimate gaming challenge of "but I might need it later" was on my mind so I hadn't fired. Then my flare died, and the wolves began inching towards me. As I fired my first shot, the other wolf broke into a sprint. I fired again and missed. Now I was fighting off a wolf with my knife and barely got it off me in time to survive. I then walked back to my cabin with a scrap of clothing still intact and blurred vision, staggering through the snow. About half a mile later I collapsed, and faded into "the long dark". This game is wonderful. The graphic style hides the low budget well and the sandbox nature meant I never felt I was retreading the same path. The surprising depth of this game kept me pushing forward, and so I would give this game a 9/10.

I've bought this game back when it was in Pre-Alpha, and even back then I didn't regret buying, even though back then there was hardly anything to do. But hell, I loved the game back then, and I still do, if it comes to any zombie survival games - this is it. None other game recreates such tactical thinking, such fear of dying as this game does, every step you make you think about the consequences, you think about where you should set your base, and what to do to protect it best, but what made this game even better was for me was the addition of MP, I've waited since alpha for the game to have Multiplayer added to the game, and I always felt like it would change the game completely, and hell, it did. Multiplayer, especially with friends, added this serious survival feel I didn't feel ever before in a game, not in DayZ, nor Rust, nor any multiplayer survival game. You care for your friend in-game, you don't want them to get injured, or worse - bitten, but you also don't want them standing, doing nothing. As a good example, I'd like to share this survivor's story:
We all assigned roles to what we'll do, one would take care of the food, another would secure the area of zombies, every once in a while we'd send out people to look for supplies, it was amazing, however, while we grew bigger, we needed better supplies, as well as some shotguns, so we decided to go to West Point, we left our home behind, hoping that we'd come back to it still being in shape...Well, at least most of it.  On the way there one of our friend's condition was getting worse - if we wouldn't find medication, he probably wouldn't make it. On the way there, we tactically dealt with zombies, or sneaked through them,  when the odds were too high, I'd fire a couple of rounds to distract a crowd of zombies, we'd get supplies at a drive-by diner and kept going, but unless we hurried - our friend wasn't going to make it, and sadly, he didn't, and it meant more than in any game, and that, is what I'd call a true survival experience. You cared that your friend died, with that one less man, not only do your possibilities go down, but so do your chances go down, every bullet you take, took and will take will make an impact, and a brilliant idea done poorly will cause the death of your team, and this is what I love about the game. While playing it, I felt like I was in some weird mix between The Last Of Us, The Walking Dead and something like Fallout, as amazing as it might be...However, I really think that there should be more of a 'leveling' system, since, even though you do have a bunch of skills to level, if you die, you quickly shake it off, I hope that the devs add something that would make you more attached to your character than you are now.
Project Zomboid is packed with features and things to do and a lot of places to go to, there are a ton of items, and a ton of items to craft, but some currently don't have any use, as mentioned, this game is still fairly early in the development, some features that aren't in the game may be fairly important to survival, for example, a generator, that you'll need to get electricity from when the power runs out, luckily water barrels are buildable, so you won't dehydrate when you run out of water. But those are some things to keep in mind.
The game is very stable right now, there are a few bugs, which is to be expected, considering the game isn't finished, but I'd recommend this game to anyway, since this game is made purely from passion and talent, and it has to be one of my favourite survival singleplayer games, and one of the best (if not the best) of survival multiplayer games, and it ain't even finished yet!

"five nights at freddys" is a game that showed up out of nowhere and rose to fame alarmingly fast, it even spawned a prequel surprisingly quickly and now a third game is on its way. while i havent played the prequel (five nights at freddys 2) quite yet, ive watched people play through the game in its entirety and i will have to say, that i will probably always prefer the original game over it. you are placed into an office setting with nothing to interact with but two doors on each side of you (complete with lights), a battery and usage meter and a moniter set up with cameras. you are immobile, you cant move, cant defend yourself in anyway. you receive a "phone call" (pre-recorded message) from a former worker, explaining to you what you are to be doing and how to use your only available equipment. you are then left alone, from 12AM to 6AM to defend yourself against the apparent "animatronic animals" that are said to be "active at night" but "harmless". turns out, once the message ends, all four of the animatronics will awaken and begin making their way to your destination. if you dont act quickly and close the doors at the right time, you will be defeated.
not only did "five nights at freddys" take horror gaming to a completely new perspective, it also has a lot of background detail that you will find difficult to not search into once you learn about it. the story of "freddy fazbears pizzaria" is still developing, everything is still unfolding, this is only the beginning.

As an experienced player of Telltale games I jumped into this title not expecting too much. Telltale have made very similar games for a few years now and they keep the concept going mostly steady. After a few letdowns with some previous titles I didn't really set my bar high for this game. However, im glad to say I was very impressed by this game and the improvement Telltale has made to this title.
This game features a good set of hard choices to make, however it's hard to say how much inpact it will have for the future, but they are really tricky and you have to stop and think for many of them. The choices (without spoiling) were most of the time pretty equal in procent between players choosing A or B, meaning that more people then me found that there was a lot of hard picks to make.
I learned a lot about the villains from another perspective in this game, like catwoman, two-face and joker before they got their role. You get the chance to try and change who they become and which you wanna help or try and become friend with. It's a very interesting perspective, especially since the other batman games only follows a set line where the villains are bad guys, while this game let you make more decisions and learn to know them better. This give you as the player more feelings for them and it's an effective way of doing story-telling.
This is a game focused on Bruce Wayne, his family legacy and a lot of things I didn't know came up. I have played all the other batman games and watched the movies, however I haven't read the comics so I still have missed a lot. Therefore it's hard for me to compare the two and whats completely new and what is taken from the comics. But this game added a lot more for me even as someone who have played previous games, as it doesn't focus as much on the joker and more about the events before the other games.
A new villain is also included in this game, which is refreshing since Joker made many appearances in the other batman games. I won't spoil who this new villain is, but let me just say its very interesting and the story takes many turns in directions I didn't see coming.
Telltale is extremely good at making you like characters to later be screwed over by them or killed. This is something they have done in previous games as well and you can roleplay as more of a good guy, evil and mean, or try and be neutral. I haven't seen Telltale make the decisions, choices and characters feel this impactful since The Walking Dead, which is a very good thing, for those of you who haven't played that title. It's very exciting and more interesting to play the Telltale's Tales From The Borderlands for example, in my opinion.
The QTE's have been improved I would say. I feel like there's less fighting in this game then the others and more focus on dialogue, but there's still a decent amount of it, so stay away if you hate QTE (quick time events - basically pushing buttons in a said order). They made it better and somehow makes it feel impactful in the fights, but of course the story is the strong point of this title.
Batman is known for solving crimes and searching for clues on crime scenes. Well like the other batman games you have some of that in this game as well. It's pretty simple but fun anyway and it's a welcome change in gameplay from just QTE's.
You can play the game with keyboard + mouse or with a controller. I played most of the game with an xbox controller since it's mostly a game you can kick back and watch, like an interactive movie where you press buttons once in a while. But whatever you choose to play with works. The game runs at 60 fps locked and I think they have improved upon the PC-port, options menu and graphics since previous games. The style is the same but some better textures for example. They also give you some more choice this time around, for example you can pick the colour of your gear which will be unique for your playthrough.
The episodes are between 1-2 hours each, the first one is always a bit longer. Five episodes in total so you are looking at about 6-10 hours, depends on how fast you figure out the clues and how much you look around. I can't say I have any complaints about this game, I'm actually very impressed! I would put this among my top Telltale games actually and give it a big recommendation to fans of point 'n' click, Telltale games in general or fans of Batman and superheroes. Love it!

This game is a really REALLY cool concept. Rhythm and platforming are 2 genres that I never expected to be this fun.
The art in this game is truly really cool, and it's unfortunate that it's moving so quickly because I really wish I could fully appreciate it all. The music is rockin', and it fits the theme of the game perfectly.
And then there's the gameplay. Sort of a love/hate relationship in my opinion. Again, the concept is awesome, but there are few things about the execution that I wanted to be more fleshed out. These minor things are marked under the game's difficulty, but at some points they were frustrating.
- The indicator to show you the next action is on the smaller side, and unless you change options it's very hard to see in some color palettes the game brings to the table.
- There were times where I thought for sure I was pressing the indicator at the right time with the music, but found out it was slightly off. This could be me not catching what beat the hits were on within the main rhythm, but very often it felt just slightly out of sync.
Any other gripe I would have about this game is nitpicking. Overall the dev did an amazing job of bringing this concept to life, and it really is a trip. Somewhat short, but amazing for completionists/perfectionists. Buy this for either a short, thrilling ride or a longer, more challenging experience.
Overall 8/10, looking forward to putting more hours in.

This is a great example of a game that's awesome, but not for everyone. I can wholeheartedly recommend it for the story aspects, the worldbuilding and the athmosphere, but there's stuff in it that can turn people off.
Let's go about the general positives first. It's a game in which you explore a marine underworld in which you'll encounter several islands, each with it's own storyline that you can follow through your travels. You'll make decisions, meet a wide variety of characters, find treasures and, most importantly, get immersed in a plethora of fascinating telltales. This, too, is where the games shines: It's immersion, it's storytelling and it's fascinating landscape of things.
However, the developers combined this exploration and storytelling aspect with a roguelike permadeath systen (that you can turn off) and a chance system (based on various skills that you can 'level up' in various ways) that can lock you out of storylines if you fail certain checks. Which can be frustrating, since you basically need to play the game multiple times to actually reach all conclusions to the stories.
Also, it's a supremely slow-paced game. You will have a lot of downtime which some people find to be far too much. Also, the combat system is not exactly stellar either.
And I can understand if people find the overall 'gameplay' aspect of the game to be tedious. Or to be unfullfilling. Or to be too slow.
If you can, however, deal with these aspects, the worldbuilding and storylines can give you much. There's a lot to love in this game. And I enjoyed every hour I spent in the Underzee.

The Testament of Sherlock Holmes is a good compromise between old-style adevnture games and new-era 3D adventure games with richer stories and cutscenes. It's also better than its sequel which emphasizes too much on the new-era style.
The variety of the puzzles is enjoyable and almost everyone is decently implemented. The good thing is that every puzzle is integrated in the scenario and not here just for the purpose or making your brain working (I do not like point and click games like Myst). The difficulty is also not too high and not too low, decently made overall even if the difficulty does not improve over time.
The gameplay is really good if you play on first person mode, OK at third person. I chose the last option because I like viewing my character but sometimes I switched to FP mode because of the limitations of the TP mode. In fact, it's harder to target a location sometimes while in TP mode. Still, it's not horrible to play, just a bit harder. I played it with both gamepad and mouse/keybord and I prefer the first option even if I'm an old PC player.
The graphics are OK technically speaking and retranscribe well the londonish atmosphere. English voices (which were impossible to pair with french subtitles - which was not a problem because I understand english - even with the developpers tips for steam version) are really well made, especially Holmes voice which retranscribes well the personality of the character.
The narrative part is nice even if some events seem far-fetched like what we can see in spectacular american movies. I enjoyed the whole plot and the narrative which is really above the pack for this type of games (without the sacrifice of the gameplay like in telltale games). The whole story is well critten and I admit I doubted about Holmes loyalty. Maybe the last chapter in the amusement park was a bit disappointing but still good.
Finally, this game is really solid. I recommend it strongly to people who enjoy a good mix between narrative and old-style puzzles. Sherlock Holmes games are really the best adventure games series nowadays  even if the last episode orientation is disturbing.

This game is a wet dream for anyone who wasn't satisfied with Tim Burton's Batman, Nolan's Dark Knight Trilogy or even Adam West's iteration.
Why?
Because it lets you be the Batman and decide the fate of the story at the same time.
Sure, this game is more about Bruce Wayne rather than his alter ego, but that doesn't take away feeling the power of being the Caped Crusader without spamming the guts of your controller to make ultimate combos as was the case with Arkham Franchise.
The Opening vigilantism takes care of your fetish for gadgets and Ninja Fighting, followed by a deep insight in the cliche tragedy of Bruce's traumatised childhood. The twist comes with Penguin which I guess though is heavily inspired by RObin Taylor's portrayal in Gotham TV Series, yet makes more sense in terms of backstory and motif.
The best feature of the game is definitely The Detective Work which not only is similar to Arkham Franchise but also reminds you another Detective Story by TellTale "The Wolf Among Us"
All in all, The game is a great homage to every good thing happened to Batman in last 20 years including Batman Animated Series, TV Series Gotham's Villains, Arkham Franchise and of course The Dark Knight Trilogy.
It's a wonderful treat that despite trying so many things, they didn't overdo any thing and found the perfect blend.
Great Job TellTale!

I bought this game becaus bLiNd is one of my favorite EDM artists.  I think this game can best be summed up as a Rage-Rythm-Platformer.  Imagine your right hand playing DDR and your left hand playing an action-platformer at the same time; now imagine that with rave music blasting and someone has a strobe light that is cycling colors going crazy in your face.  That is what playing Klang is like.  If you think that sounds cool (and it is) there are some things to consider first.
I did beat the game on normal but this game is difficult.  Unfortunately I feel like a lot of the difficulty is artificial and comes more from the volume of audio and visual noise tripping up your brain as you're trying to multitask.  Again, it's like playing DDR but you're also having to maneuver your character around on platforms and/or constantly dodging beams that either insta-kill you or cause an obscene amount of damage.  To make matters worse, when you get a combo above a certain amount it changes the color scheme of everything on screen so by the time you readjust you're likely to be taking damage and drop the combo (ironically taking you back to the color scheme you just left as well).  A lot of the time I would die and not even realize what killed me due to the sheer amount of crap on the screen whizzing by (looking at you Angel boss).  The bosses in general are just a mess and I actually found it easier to fight them when I turned the game sound off.  That should never happen in a rythm-based game.
There were also some technical issues as well.  The cutscenes, though beautiful, would experience lag spikes even though the game itself was fine.  Platforms in levels that are programmed to fall so you don't wait on them too long would sometimes instantly fall without giving the player a chance to move but other times would give you the normal 1-2 second window to actually keep moving.  I actually soft-locked the game once by skipping a cutscene.  Luckily there was a checkpoint right at the start of the cutscene but still...
Despite all this I have to give the game its due.  The soundtrack is FANTASTIC, bLiNd really outdid himself on this project and you can actually unlock the music tracks if you just want to listen to them later on.  Visually the game is beautiful with vibrant colors that really draw you into this weird rave world.  The story makes no sense but that seems intentional and I honestly didn't mind it being left open to interpretation; I kind of got a God of War feel from it honestly.  While short it should provide enough of a challenge to keep people playing for hours on end to even just finish it.
The gameplay is pretty good overall as well.  Somehow Tinimations turned DDR into an action-platformer and made it work well.  The controls were pretty responsive and apart from some parts where I questioned a hitbox and the slide mechanic, it handled better than some AAA games I've played that also rely on controls being precise.  The wall jump mechanic is pretty cool as well and it enabled the game to do some pretty interesting and diverse things in the levels.  And while I did slag off on the mess of visuals a little bit ago there are levels that are much more just about hitting the "notes" or hitting the "notes" with just a little bit of platforming thrown in and these are great.
I feel as though if some of the visual mess were to be toned down and some of the death beams ease up a little, this game would be a definite recommendation by me to anyone.  As it stands though, while I did enjoy it overall there are parts I never want to play again, chief among these are the bosses.  If you like EDM music and want a novel game that will challenge you and maybe make you frustrated, give it a shot.

Note: Don't pay attention to my played time, as the game is only ~12 hours long.
The Testament of Sherlock Holmes starts off very, very poorly. Thankfully, the game quickly improves and turns into a fairly interesting Sherlock Holmes mystery which is very reminiscent of some of the original tales. Just please, skip the painful cutscenes with the creepy attic children.
Keep in mind that while there are a few "deduction boards" and puzzles that require deduction, that this is primarily a fairly traditional adventure game. Expect lots of running around, trying to find the random items that the game has decided you should be able to pick up, and then the using of those items (sometimes after some combining) on various locations. Also present are a fair number of (mostly) generic "toy" puzzles, some of which you've probably seen before if you've played any Professor Layton/mobile puzzle games. Think (very basic) chess-themed puzzles, unraveling a bunch of "tangled" ropes, or determining which person is in which position (based on a set of hints).
While the game is far from perfect, and there are definitely some awkward moments within, it's overall a fairly enjoyable mystery-themed adventure game.

A lot of gamers rant and rave about how scary Five Nights At Freddy's is, but I guess I just don't see it. What it comes down to is that it's a stress management game. It tries to get in your head. Really you could simply wait around until you see the face of a character flash on either side of the room, then close the door. But the game uses atmosphere and sound to make you anxious, causing you to look at the cameras, taking your eyes off the doors and draining the power of your backup battery.
It is an interesting game and fun to give a try, but ultimately it's based on making the player anxious and causing jump scares.

I am a huge fan of the novels and short stories, and previous PC titles such as The Serrated Scalpel and The Case of the Rose Tattoo, but I cannot recommend this. The writing is clumsy and the dialogue moves from acceptable to laughable. Some textures look fine, while others look decades old. The lighting is poor, the lip-syncing is terrible, and the locations feel like movie sets rather Victorian London.
There are only 3-4 deduction board sequences and their questions are either ridiculously easy or you are not provided with enough information (for example, the information you are given to solve it matches several of the possible answers). There is no penalty for guessing wrong, so you just answer the easy ones and guess on the others until they're correct. Most of the puzzles in the game are combination puzzles. It is absolutely laughable how many people in 19th Century London owned puzzle lock boxes, I think 1 in 2 NPCs in this game have one. The game begins to take the♥♥♥♥♥♥when a door in the sewers has a puzzle lock. There are also some very silly padding sequences, like when you are given control of Toby the bloodhound.
It is often condescending, provides an insulting portrayal of Holmes and Watson, and is just generally a very poor game. I should have stayed away from these 3D Holmes games after the first two were so bad. I miss the old Mythos Software series.

Overall, a disappointment. This is less a game - more of a stylized interactive comic book. The toughest challenge was to stay awake through some of the dialog - just to get to an interactive part of the game. Check YouTube gameplay videos before purchasing to see if this is what you want.

While a creative combination Klang's two components (platforming and rhythm games) are sometimes at odds. When it works well it's a frenetic combination with appealing visuals and an aural delight, but the soundtrack can make reading a strong rhythm difficult, filtering visual input can be a real pain with the intense trippy visuals, and at its worst Klang feels like trying to simultaneously play two very different games at the same time, rather than a seamless fusion. Especially when an option to help you recover and not be punished MORE for faltering once is turned off by default. Also, don't expect a story to match the fun tunes, interesting character design and visual polish. It's an interesting ride, but hardly worth mentioning there even is a premise.
If the concept of the combination has you intrigued, check this one out, but I'd recommend considering turning on "Reflex mode" (slow mo when you miss a 'klang' - the game's DDR arrow projectiles) and actually give "casual" difficulty a second thought if you're not confident in both your platforming and rhythm game skills. I beat the game on normal in an evening, (~3.6 hours) but the challenging bits felt more frustrating than a rewarding challenge to overcome, and the post-story challenges were demoralizing without dropping to casual. Again, having Reflex mode on lessened this effect, since it provides a sorely needed recovery mechanism, rather than failure leading to several consequences that made missing the next action more likely.
An imperfect execution, but a marvelous idea and a neat new genre fusion none the less.

This is my review. I am a veteran player who stopped playing this game a long while ago... until I saw it on steam!
MY STORY:
I was a CS2D fan for a long time. Back then, I was such a poor fellow that couldn't afford any game! So it was either piracy or a freeware game. For most of us, those were the only options. So I stood by this game for many years, playing role play prison servers, custom zombie servers and so much more... This game used to be filled with players back then, but slowly the players started to move away from CS2D. As every year goes by, a massive amount of players drift away. Sad... until Unreal Software got this onto Steam! When I saw this on the free to play section I jumped out of my seat, amazed that such a game like this made it into the store! I quickly installed it (I haven't played the game in years) and I was amazed by how much they've done with the game.
There's now dynamic lighting, 3D walls (even though it would mess up the name of the game), a better modding support, HD skins and textures (that were taken from the CS2D forums community), revamped maps, widescreen support and so much more. You can tell the people behind this game really were dedicated.
So, those being said let's get into the review!
I will split them into PROs and CONs
PROs:
• Revived community - Thank god for Steam.
• Frequent updates
• Anti-cheat system
• A very user friendly map maker
• Free!!!
• Custom sprays are back
• So many custom gamemodes
• Some extra fun deathmatch weapons and items: chainsaw, lazergun, grenadelauncher, satchel charge, RPG, air-strike, super armor, machete, etc.
• Easy to mod
Unfortunatly, this isn't the best game ever. Not even the best free game ever. But I still apreciate it to this day.
CONs:
• Awful gunplay (Almost NO stratergy)
• Unfair weapons/over powered weapons
• Low field of view (people always have to guess where the enemy is from far away)
• Really stupid bots that either instantly reacts to you or not even see you at all!

The game of Evolve pulls you into the future where mankind employs high tech hunters to purge planets of alien life forms that may be a threat to them. Paving the way for human expansion or at least that was what seemed to be conveyed to me while playing this game. On the main page for evolve there is no real story involved. Merely fluff like "man vs nature".
Obviously they felt there shouldn't be much of a story. No compelling back stories on the hunters or even how the Kraken misses its long lost love which made it lash out at the humans moving in on his backyard or how the Goliath longs for a little human named George or was it a rabbit?
This game was a lot of fun initially. Whether I was the monster or a hunter. The monster player will run away from the hunters, upon reaching stage 2 the monster would engage the hunters. Testing their resolve to the chase. Fleeing when the monster has taken more damage than it is comfortable with.
In the role of the hunter, you will need to pursue and damage the monster before it has a chance to evolve. The best stage to kill the monster is evolutionary stage one. At stage two, the monster will be a hand full and at stage 3 the hunters will be in for one hell of a fight.
I was so looking forward to this game. Yes, one could say that I was hyped. Until I played it for a few hours. Then I started to realize that it was fun but there needed to be more to this game. The only event that really forces the hunters and monster into a fight is the power relay. A few times when I was playing the monster, I evaded the hunters the entire match. The hunters were hot on my heels and as soon as I was able to attack the power relay by evolving. I made a B line for my objective, out running the hunters and destroyed the power relay before they are able to interrupt my animation of destroying it.
As a hunter, I played a couple of matches where the monster player evaded the entire time. This turned the match into a 15 minute jet pack simulator. Even with being able to double tap the jump button (This would launch you forward eating up extra fuel but allowing you to cover more ground.) I was always barely out of range to dome the monster. Some monster players are just more mobile than others, they pay attention to where the hunters are and try not to be in one location for too long. Chasing a monster for 20 minutes can become boring and if hunters are tired of the chase from the start. They can just wait at the power relay while the monster reaches its full potential.
I have a feeling that this will be the game at release, I have play tested a lot of titles in alpha and beta. Game play doesn't typically change a lot.

I enjoy playing this game. Hunter or Monster... it is fun. The majority of the time I win the match. But because of how simple the game setting is I can't throw money at it. Hunters chase monster or defend point from the monster. There are 5 players involved. One player plays the monster and four players are hunters. Each character have different abilities for the most part. The monster runs around eating animals it has killed or that are dead to gain experience to evolve (aka level up). Maximum monster level is 3.  The hunters do not level. What you see is what you get.
There is currently only 2 maps from what I could tell. With random weather effects. Once the monster is level 3 it is able to attack a power relay. Why? Who knows.... he just wants to destroy something. Plus this forces the fight to one area. There is a timer that will expire in favor of the hunters if the monster does not kill the hunters (If any one Hunter character including Daisy dog lives for a certain amount of time the dead Hunters will respawn.) or if the monster fails to destroy the power relay. This is so that the monster doesn't simply run around the map for an hour evading the hunters.
The overall plan for this title seems to be the same as what we are currently exposed to in game. DLC is planned to add additional monsters. Hopefully additional characters and maps will be provided with said DLC along with new game modes. Only having an arena style mode on a jungle like map or any other map will get old pretty fast. Especially since there is only 1 person as a monster. Don't get me wrong, I like the concept. But I already found myself asking "Will my play time on this title rival Left 4 Dead?"
In L4D I had 339 hours played and in L4D2 I clocked in 466 hours. One could say I played the diddly out of those titles. So will this title hold the same interest that those had? Why the benchmark? Because this is the same studio that created L4D. I found that my question was answered the first night of the alpha when I stopped playing. The only reason I had stopped was merely because the novelty of the concept was wearing off.
I played it the next day with friends. But even they were questioning the longevity of Evolve. We came up with a number. Odds are (if it remained as it is currently) we would only play it for a couple of weeks and then move on to the next game. I am sure others would not agree with my conclusion. But this is what would happen if I purchased this at release.  In the current day of gaming, I need a game more compelling and challenging to keep me engaged for a long period.
L4D was pretty simple you say? But there were more dynamics involved. When playing as a survivor everything wanted to eat your face and you had 4 players playing unique infected.  There were trigger events that would increase the danger.  In Evolve, the Hunters just run past 99% of the environment without a real issue. Minus the trapping creatures that pop up once in a while. On the monster side of things he simply kills what he can and eats for xp. It's too simple, I need more from this game in its current state.
PS: Please don't even get me started on the progression system, Daisy still needs to lick up 4 people from dying in order for my Trapper to unlock further areas of her skills.

Ah, Project Zombid. I have been a follower of this scince the beginning back in 2011. I have been with this with the Early Tech Demo, then to Desura, and now onto steam. And I would say, I am pleased. I am VERY pleased to see where Project Zomboid has gone over the past three years in a half years. Multiplayer used to be a hope of happening and a myth. Now we actually have it! Project Zomboid is a dream game to me, it gives survival to the apocalypse. Now I am sure you are tired of me reminiscing about the "days of old" so lets get to the review.
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
WHAT IS PROJECT ZOMBOID? Project Zomboid is a basically a open world replica of the small towns of Muldraugh and West Point in the state of Keuntucky. More areas are soon to come I belive such as another small town named Bedord, but I have high hopes that bigger towns such as Louisville are to come. Now to story is that you are a survivor in this area and "you guessed it" zombies started coming. The county is under quaratine so there is no way in or out, but it wont hold forever so adventually after a couple weeks or months in game time you should go further into the world. You start off with nothing but the clothes on your back and you go out and gear up to survive, either building yourself a fort at the local spiffos or live off the land on a quiet farm far away from the towns and farm tomatos and cabbage. However, because NPCs have not been implmented yet there is nobody but you to loot all the houses. So pretty much the whole county is for your pickens. Multiplayer which has only recently been added ----Quote from 3/3/14 for any future readers---- really adds a much greater sense of difficulty. Also multiplayer adds a much greater atmosphere, windows are shatered, barren stores with all the food cleaned off the counter, and I only hope that they will add a feature that over time grass will grow up in the streets. But you catch my drift here. Also if you are worried about this being about Dayz or Rust where the game is ruined by terrible people, the people in this is much more well mannered, but you should still be cautious for you can never quite know who is your friend and who is your enemey. Sense PVP is a bit akward in the current combat system it is a little difficult in my opinon. The only time I was killed was when I was in my fort with my friend and I was broadcasting that we had an infinte supply of food (we did) and we can supply protection (we had hundreds of bullets and dozens of guns and melee weapons) but the new survivor that came stole our shotgun and shot us so... But you live and you learn you know? Next time you be more cautious and maybe set up shop in a farm in the countryside away from the cities. So basically is you are worried about this games multiplayer being ruined by terrible people, dont. Anyways, multiplayer is still in development but singleplayer still offers a bunch of features, although once you get everything you need you can basically survive forever and this can get sorta boring until NPCs are added. This is why multiplayer was such a good choice because of that fact you have other people to survive with and you can form a group and try and rebuild.
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
THE GOOD----
*The zombies are a challenge here. With whatever weapon you have it could take you from 15 to 20+ hits to dispatch one or just 1 hit if you have an axe. Basically if you have a spoon or a fork, this is not the best weapon to use. But you dont want to go into combat if not necessary, because you can easily screw up and get yourself bit or scratched. Scratched is 25% and bit is I belive 92% chance, the reason why it is not 100% is that it gives you hope that you would live and survive. If you are planing on clearing out an area though you would want to be well armed firearms and melee weapons.
*Hunger, Thirst, Sleep (singleplayer only), Sickness, etc.... Sense this is survival, it is not JUST the walkers you are fighting. It is your mind, body, and soul! Sadness and bordem can effect you and so can your physical needs. There is not a whole lot to talk about this so yeah.
*Crafting/Buidling. This is a awsome feature in my opinon. This allows you to fortify your home or current dwelling, for permenant or just for the night. Again not a whole lot to talk about this so let that be that.
*Isometric View. Some people may not be a fan of the isometric view but I think it gives the game a ceartin feel that most games dont have. The top down perspective is something not everyone will love but I myself like it. But even if you dont like it it is not jerky or anything that will effect your game or your play experince.
*Multiplayer. This is still very early but I have high hopes for multiplayers future and further development. This gives the game a much deeper feel and it is full with good people. From atleast what I see that is.
*NPCS (soon to come) NPCS are not in the game yet but they are soon to come, I am exicted for this because the developers have been working hard on the lines and writing for NPCS. This should be great news for people who think multiplayer is not the callings card.
_______________________________________________________________________________________
THE BAD---
*When you build a fort and have all the food and water you need, whats the point in playing? Thankfully multiplayer and NPCs are going to make up for this.
*Maybe a bug here and there. Although I do not think I have seen any.
*LONG and I mean LOOOONG run times between towns. Now when I said before that this was a replica of the county, I was not kidding. This run times may be a little too long and are somewhat tedious and superfluous.
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
THE UGLY-----
.Get bored and go out to hunt some walkers and then get devoured by the walkers.
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
So over all it is a 8.5/10 for me. It has its fair share of problems and you may have to be in the mood to play it but once you do, it can offer you alot of fun. I was thinking about a 9 but when you got down to the surface, it is sorta barren. But this is still a great game in which I recommend to anybody who likes some humanity and survival in their zombie game!

Pretty nice hidden object game with a lovely aesthetic and some decent mini-game puzzles, but with janky controls and a nonexistent story. Worth it at a low price for fans of the genre.
Morphopolis is a pretty hidden object game. If you do not like hidden object games, do not buy. You play as various iterations of insects that are moving through the world at a very slow pace for… some reason. As far as I can tell there is no story to the game, just a series of hidden object games and mini-puzzles set in a relatively pretty world. For me that was fine.
My biggest problem with the game was the awful movement controls. You hold down the mouse courser to move instead of just clicking; this results in some awkward dancing and can lead you to incorrectly assume that you cannot move further along a path. The movement is also way too slow and there is no option to double click to change scenes quickly, which artificially prolongs the game by forcing you to crawl back and forth between scenes.
The game also does a relatively poor job of explaining the mini-game puzzle rules as well as some important mechanics which can lead to some frustration. For example you can click on your own character which will is essential to reveal items in some chapters, but as far as I know that is never mentioned in the tutorial.
Still, if you can get it cheap (I got it as part of the art appreciation pack for 0.44 Euro) and you like hidden object games, why not? It’s not a great game, but it was worth the two hours I spent on it.

Easily one of the best zombie survival sandbox games. The graphics can put some people off, but they fit the style of the game quite well. There's a decent amount of variety with the zombies, although don't expect evey single thing to be unique. Character customization is just enough to provide a dash of flavour to each character you make (you WILL make many).
Sound isn't too bad. Most of the sounds are good enough for you to get immersed into the world. There are some glitches with the sound I have noticed, such as a zombie screaming really loud 15 times in a second. But i've only came across that one time so far. The soundtrack, however, is absoultely amazing in my opinion. The music changes to what is going on in the game. If you're breaking into a house and the alarm goes off (which can happen often) the music takes a dramatic turn as the zombies start to form a horde around the house. Gets even more dramatic when you're running from the hordes
The controls of the game are pretty simple and comfortable, yet can feel... Clunky, i would say, at times. You use the WASD keys to move (of course), mouse to click objects to search them, Ctrl for your attacks. Now the reason I say they're clunky at times is that you can use the E key to interact with objects such as hurdling a fence or climbing through a window. However, sometimes when you press the key it doesn't do what you hoped for. Example: I was running through a house i had cleared earlier to lose a horde, i ran to the window that was open hit E and my character closes the window instead of hopping through. Panicked i kept hitting E instead of right clicking for the little drop-down menu... Needless to say, that character passed away due to 30 zombies eating his flesh. Plus you can get caught up on an object here and there if you're not paying attention. (i.e forcing running yourself into a kitchen counter to close a window, only to get stuck.)
There's plenty to do in the game itself and you'll quickly find yourself doing a little narrative of your character as you play. Characters have their own "wants" in a way. They will become bored, they will get tired, they will get hungry and they will get sick but it makes you care that much more about them. You want them to have a book to read to stay sane or have some smokes/liqour around to keep the stress down because you find yourself doing what you said you'd do in a zombie apocalypse with your friends in a cloudy room... Then you discover how much of an idiot you were when food runs out, power/water stops running, and you have zombies surrounding you. You can build your own little fort, furniture, barricades... hell you can even farm! Haven't dabbled with the farming bit yet as that's not my natural play style.
Now keep in mind, this game is Early Access still and I haven't even scratched the surface of this game myself. There will be bugs that you might run into that others did not. Features may recieve tweaks, fixes or may be outright removed/added. So do keep that in mind when you buy.
Overall, this game is well worth the asking price. I may only have a small amount of hours in the game, but it is easily a new top 10 favorite. If you can handle a game that gives you no objective whatsoever to have fun, this is right up your alley whether you have 20 minutes spare time or 20 hours a day.

This is a great example of a game that's awesome, but not for everyone. I can wholeheartedly recommend it for the story aspects, the worldbuilding and the athmosphere, but there's stuff in it that can turn people off.
Let's go about the general positives first. It's a game in which you explore a marine underworld in which you'll encounter several islands, each with it's own storyline that you can follow through your travels. You'll make decisions, meet a wide variety of characters, find treasures and, most importantly, get immersed in a plethora of fascinating telltales. This, too, is where the games shines: It's immersion, it's storytelling and it's fascinating landscape of things.
However, the developers combined this exploration and storytelling aspect with a roguelike permadeath systen (that you can turn off) and a chance system (based on various skills that you can 'level up' in various ways) that can lock you out of storylines if you fail certain checks. Which can be frustrating, since you basically need to play the game multiple times to actually reach all conclusions to the stories.
Also, it's a supremely slow-paced game. You will have a lot of downtime which some people find to be far too much. Also, the combat system is not exactly stellar either.
And I can understand if people find the overall 'gameplay' aspect of the game to be tedious. Or to be unfullfilling. Or to be too slow.
If you can, however, deal with these aspects, the worldbuilding and storylines can give you much. There's a lot to love in this game. And I enjoyed every hour I spent in the Underzee.
